INSL.name: Insulator
behaviour: No custom Update function; pure static solid
HeatConduct 0 blocks heat transfer through it
Blocks electricity (no PROP_CONDUCTS), radiation, and neutrons per its own flags
Flammable=7 means other elements' fire-ignition code can still ignite it (very slowly)
builder_notes: Use as a heat/electricity/radiation break between circuits or reactors
Not literally fireproof - has nonzero Flammable so intense fire can still catch it
No self reactions; all behavior driven by neighboring elements' own code

METL.name: Metal
behaviour: No custom Update function; conducts electricity and melts via generic engine transition
Melts to LAVA (ctype METL implied by generic transition) above 1273K
PROP_HOT_GLOW: glows visibly when hot
PROP_LIFE_DEC: life counts down by 1/frame if life>0 (unused by default life=0)
builder_notes: High HeatConduct (251/255) makes it an excellent heat spreader for circuits
Very low Hardness (1) - drills/erodes easily despite being a solid
Will melt into lava if any adjacent heat source pushes it past 1273K

TUNG.name: Tungsten

props.tmp3: stores previous frame's local chamber pressure*64 (int); compared each frame to detect a swing >32/<-32 which converts TUNG to BRMT (see TUNG.cpp:L105-114, TUNG.cpp:L143-146 for initialization in create())

reacts.result: forces melt/explosion path even below normal melting point

reacts.also: occurs instead of melting this frame
reacts.cond: temp>3695K (HighTemperature field, checked in code not via engine transition) or O2-splode, then chance(1,50)

reacts.also: life set random 0-499
reacts.cond: melt-trigger condition met, not the 1/50 branch

reacts.also: random velocity kick added; if triggered by O2-splode, temp bumped by +200..+799 above melting point
reacts.cond: melt-trigger condition met, not the 1/50 or 1/100 branches
local pressure*64 changes by more than +-32 from the value recorded last frame (tmp3)

behaviour: Extremely high melting point (3695K) tracked as a Lua-editable field but applied in code, not via engine HighTemperature transition
Adjacent O2 above 2400K forces an explosive melt even before reaching 3695K
Melting outcome is randomized: mostly becomes molten LAVA(TUNG), sometimes flashes to FIRE, sometimes just spikes local pressure
Sudden local pressure swings alone (no heat) can shatter it into BRMT (brittle metal)
builder_notes: Treat as a high-temp fuse: near-immune to normal heat but O2 contact drastically lowers its failure point
Don't rely on TUNG staying solid near volatile pressure sources - it cracks into BRMT on pressure spikes
Melting is probabilistic per-frame once triggered, not instantaneous - expect a few frames of flicker

BANG.name: TNT

props.tmp: fuse/detonation state machine: 0=armed/unlit, 1=ignited this frame, 2=flood-filled to whole connected TNT block, 3=about to detonate next frame

reacts.result: entire connected TNT block synchronized to detonate together
reacts.also: uses flood_prop to set tmp=2 on all directly-connected BANG particles
local pressure += 0.5; temp set to ~MAX_TEMP/4 + original temp
life set 500-549; temp set to ~MAX_TEMP/4 + original temp
life=50, temp ~MAX_TEMP/3 + original temp, random velocity

reacts.cond: detonation frame, none of the above triggered

behaviour: Arms at 673K or on contact with FIRE/PLSM/SPRK/LIGH
All directly-connected TNT particles are flood-filled to detonate simultaneously (the 'all at once' in its description)
Detonation always occurs exactly 2 frames after ignition (tmp: 1->2->3->explode)
Result of each detonating particle is randomized between FIRE, SMKE, EMBR, or nothing
builder_notes: Wire an entire TNT structure together (touching particles) to get a simultaneous, single-frame blast
Detonation has a fixed 2-frame delay after the trigger reaches any part of the block
No blast-radius destruction is coded in BANG itself - only via the FIRE/EMBR/pressure it spawns

BOMB.name: Bomb

reacts.result: detonates: kills self, kills all particles in radius-8 circle (excluding DMND/CLNE/PCLN/BCLN/VIBR), fills that radius with EMBR (life=2, temp=MAX_TEMP), and spawns a ring of EMBR (life=50, temp=MAX_TEMP, random velocity) into empty cells out to radius 9
reacts.also: local pressure += 0.1 per particle killed

behaviour: Detonates the instant it touches almost anything (very unstable)
Blast radius 8 kills everything and fills the crater with hot EMBR sparks
A slightly larger radius-9 shell also gets EMBR sparks flung into empty space
DMND, CLNE, PCLN, BCLN, VIBR (and other BOMB/EMBR) are immune and won't trigger or be destroyed by it
builder_notes: Never let it touch structural material you want to keep - almost everything within radius 8 dies
Use CLNE/PCLN/BCLN/DMND/VIBR as blast-proof containment or triggers since they're explicitly exempted
Graphics uses PMODE_FLARE so it visually glows before detonation triggers

C5.name: C-5 (cold explosive)

props.ctype: when nonzero, a queued PHOT wavelength/color value to re-emit as a photon
props.tmp: packed photon velocity: low 16 bits = vx*255 (signed), high 16 bits = vy*255
props.tmp2: packed photon sub-pixel offset: low 16 bits = dx*255, high 16 bits = dy*255
props.life: countdown; when it reaches 0 while ctype is set, the queued PHOT is emitted

reacts.with: any particle colder than 100K (that isn't a heat insulator) or PT_CFLM
reacts.also: both self and triggering neighbor's temp set to 0K; self life set 50-199; local pressure += 1.5
PHOT inherits ctype (color/wavelength), position offset, velocity, and temp from the stored fields; C5's ctype/tmp/tmp2 reset to 0

behaviour: Set off by cold, not heat - any sub-100K neighbor (or existing CFLM) triggers conversion to cold-flame (CFLM)
Also doubles as a photon delay/relay element that can queue and later emit a PHOT with stored velocity/offset/color
Photon-relay purpose/trigger for setting ctype/tmp/tmp2 is not defined in this file (set by external code)
PROP_PHOTPASS lets light pass through it like glass
builder_notes: Chill any part of a C5 charge (ICEI, cold gas, etc.) to set it off - fire will NOT trigger it
The photon-relay behavior is inert unless something else populates ctype/tmp/tmp2 first
Cold conversion is per-neighbor probabilistic (1/6), so large charges ignite gradually, not instantly

CFLM.name: Cold Flame

props.life: randomized 50-199 on creation; drives flame color via a color table (life/2 index); decremented by PROP_LIFE_DEC, particle dies at 0 via PROP_LIFE_KILL

behaviour: No custom Update function - relies purely on generic gas movement plus LIFE_DEC/LIFE_KILL decay
Spawns with temp fixed at 0K and life randomized 50-199
Purely cosmetic/byproduct gas; all reactions that create it live in other elements' files (e.g. C5)
Rises slightly (negative Gravity -0.1) and diffuses like a light gas
builder_notes: Short-lived (life 50-199 frames) - don't expect it to persist for storage or logic
Has no independent ignition/reaction behavior of its own; it's an explosion/reaction byproduct
Cold (0K spawn temp) - can chill adjacent elements via normal heat exchange, not via special code

DEST.name: Destruction (Dest)

props.life: decays from a random 30-49 (reset whenever it hits <=0 or exceeds 37); reduced by 4 (x3 if the destroyed target is TYPE_SOLID) each time it destroys something; PROP_LIFE_KILL_DEC kills DEST when this hits <=0

reacts.cond: the single randomly-picked neighbor within radius 2 is one of these

reacts.also: target's temp set to MAX_TEMP; local pressure += 20 (+10 more if NEUT spawned); self life -= 4
self life -= 4 (x3 if target is TYPE_SOLID), clamped to minimum 1

reacts.result: target's temp set to MAX_TEMP (not killed)
reacts.cond: same as above, the other 2/3 of the time

behaviour: Each frame picks one random cell within a radius-2 box and attacks it (not all neighbors at once)
Own temp is forced to MAX_TEMP every frame and local pressure steadily rises (+80/frame, clamped)
Destroys roughly 1/3 of targets outright per hit, heats the rest without destroying them
PLUT/DEUT neighbors specifically get converted into NEUT (neutron generator effect)
Immune to and ignores DEST, DMND, BCLN, CLNE, PCLN, PBCN
builder_notes: Far more destructive than BOMB per the in-game description - breaks through nearly anything except a short immunity list
Radius of effect is only ~2 px per frame but constant and relentless while life>0
Useful as a slow neutron source when placed against PLUT or DEUT
Self-destructs (life hits 0) faster when it destroys TYPE_SOLID targets (3x life cost)

EMBR.name: Embers

props.ctype: packed RGB color (0xRRGGBB) inherited from the explosion/firework that spawned it, used for tinting
props.tmp: render-mode tag: 0 = plain fading spark, 1 = glow/blend mode (fireworks-style), 2 = flat bright flash (blast-style)
props.life: default 50; counts down (PROP_LIFE_DEC) and the particle is destroyed at 0 (PROP_LIFE_KILL); also drives fade brightness in graphics

behaviour: Represents flying/settling sparks produced by explosions (BANG, BOMB, FIRW, FWRK, IGNT)
Dies instantly when it touches ordinary solid/powder/liquid matter that doesn't allow spark-settling
Can safely rest on other spark-settling materials (e.g. other EMBR, certain wires)
Color and glow style depend entirely on ctype/tmp set by whatever created it
builder_notes: Don't expect EMBR to accumulate on plain ground - it self-destructs unless the surface has PROP_SPARKSETTLE
It's purely a visual/thermal byproduct with no reactions of its own beyond the settle-check
Its default spawn temp is very hot (~500C) - it can ignite flammable material it lands near (via that material's own fire-catch logic)

FIRE.name: Fire

props.ctype: carries an inherited type/tag via CarriesTypeIn(FIELD_CTYPE); set to PT_FIRE on the WTRV it produces when burning out via combustion
props.tmp: low 2 bits act as a combined O2/H2-absorption flag; when both bits are set (value 3) the FIRE converts to WTRV (exact bit-setting code lives outside this file)
props.life: spawned at 120-169; at <=1, converts to WTRV (if tmp&3==3) or SMKE (if temp<625K)

reacts.also: neighbor temp set to FIRE's default temp + Flammable/2; life set 180-259; local pressure += 0.25*CFDS if neighbor is Explosive
reacts.cond: neighbor is in open space (surround_space) or is itself Explosive; excludes SPRK igniting RBDM/LRBD/INSL, PHOT igniting INSL, and SPNG unless its life==0

reacts.result: THRM converts to LAVA (ctype BMTL, temp 3500K) or LAVA (ctype THRM, life 400, tmp 20, temp 3500K)
reacts.also: local pressure += 50 in the BMTL branch

reacts.result: target's life reduced to 99 (starts it smoldering)

reacts.cond: life<=1 and tmp low-2-bits==3 (interpreted as complete O2+H2 combustion)

reacts.also: life set 250-269
reacts.cond: life<=1 and temp<625K and not the O2+H2 case above

reacts.result: target converts to LAVA (ctype=target's type, or GLAS for SAND, or BMTL for BRMT)
reacts.also: target life set 240-359
reacts.cond: legacy_enable on; excludes METL/IRON/ETRD/PSCN/NSCN/NTCT/PTCT/BMTL/BRMT/SALT/INWR being melted by FIRE specifically

reacts.result: target converts to WATR; FIRE itself is extinguished (killed)
target killed; FIRE itself is extinguished (killed)

behaviour: Ignites virtually any Flammable-rated neighbor, with odds scaled by both Flammable value and local pressure
Burns out into SMKE when cool (<625K) or into WTRV when it has fully combined O2+H2
In legacy heat-transfer mode, water (WATR/DSTW/SLTW/ICEI/SNOW) extinguishes FIRE on contact
Update function is shared code also used by PLSM and LAVA elements for their own transformations (not detailed here)
Converts to PLSM if heated above 2773K
builder_notes: Ignition chance depends on both the target's Flammable stat and ambient pressure - high pressure spreads fire faster
Water-based liquids/ices will snuff FIRE out only when legacy heat simulation is enabled
Don't expect FIRE to melt METL/IRON/PSCN/NSCN/etc directly - those need hotter sources like LAVA

FIRW.name: Fireworks

props.tmp: 0 = unlit fuse; 1 = lit and flying toward apex; 2 = detonating this frame
props.life: while tmp==1: counts down from a random 20-29 before detonation; reset to a fresh 70-109 on each spawned EMBR fragment

reacts.result: ignites (tmp=1) and launches upward/away from gravity
reacts.also: life set 20-29; velocity impulse applied opposite the local gravity direction

reacts.result: explodes into 40 EMBR particles with a shared random color
reacts.also: each EMBR gets tmp=1 (glow mode), life 70-109, temp 5750-6249K, inherits half the FIRW's velocity plus random spread; local pressure += 8; FIRW is destroyed
reacts.cond: tmp has reached its detonate state (tmp>=2)

behaviour: Ignited only by direct contact with FIRE, PLSM, or THDR (lightning)
Launches itself away from the local gravity direction once lit, like a bottle rocket
Detonates into a 40-particle colorful EMBR burst after a short random flight
Fuse timing (20-29 frames) and color are randomized every launch
builder_notes: Needs direct FIRE/PLSM/THDR contact to launch - ambient heat alone will not set it off
Trajectory follows the ambient gravity field, so custom gravity setups redirect the launch angle
Produces a visible pressure pulse (+8) at the burst point, useful as a pressure trigger

FSEP.name: Fuse Powder

props.life: default 50; burn timer - decremented while <40; at <=0 the particle becomes PLSM; jumps to 39 to start burning when ignited

reacts.result: self converts to PLSM (life set to 50)
spawns a nearby PLSM (life 50) while still burning
life set to 39 (starts the burn countdown)
reacts.cond: unburned (life>40), neighbor within radius 2 is SPRK OR self is hot enough

behaviour: Burns slowly like FUSE but as a loose powder instead of a solid strand
Ignites from adjacent SPRK or from being heated above ~400C
While burning, periodically vents small PLSM sparks before finally becoming PLSM
Powder form means it can fall/settle unlike the rigid FUSE
builder_notes: Good for a loose/poured fuse trail rather than a fixed wire path
Ignition is probabilistic (1/15 per neighbor per frame) - a single SPRK touch isn't guaranteed instant ignition
Ends its burn by becoming PLSM, not FIRE - plan pressure/heat effects accordingly

FUSE.name: Fuse

props.tmp: insulation/length counter, default 50; decremented toward 0 while burning; forced to 39 by ignition or capped at 39 under high pressure; converts self to FSEP at 0
props.life: burn timer, default 50; decremented while <40; spawns PLSM sparks while burning; converts self to PLSM at <=0

reacts.result: self converts to PLSM (life set to 50)
spawns a nearby PLSM (life 50) while burning

reacts.cond: neighbor within radius 2 is SPRK, or self is very hot, and life>40
reacts.chance: SPRK: always on contact; hot-temp case: 1/20

behaviour: Burns slowly along its length like a classic fuse, igniting from SPRK or extreme heat (>700C)
High local pressure erodes its remaining fuse length (tmp) faster
When its insulation (tmp) runs out, it crumbles into loose FSEP powder before finishing its burn
Emits occasional PLSM sparks while actively burning, then finally becomes PLSM
builder_notes: Rigid solid form is good for a fixed fuse line through a structure
High ambient pressure (>2.7) will degrade it into FSEP mid-burn - avoid pressurized fuse runs
SPRK ignition is guaranteed on contact, unlike the probabilistic heat-based ignition

FWRK.name: Fireworks (legacy)

props.ctype: 0 normally; set to PT_DUST by external code (e.g. NEUT interactions elsewhere) to force immediate launch; briefly holds a packed RGB color for its EMBR burst
props.life: 0 = unlaunched; set to 18-27 once launched; 1-2 triggers the explosion burst; reset to 0 if it ever reaches >=45 without exploding

reacts.result: launches (life set 18-27) and gets a velocity impulse opposite local gravity
reacts.cond: life==0 AND ((in open space (surround_space) and temp>400K, probabilistic) OR ctype==PT_DUST)
reacts.chance: chance(9 + temp/40, 100000) for the heat path; always for the ctype==DUST path

reacts.result: explodes into 40 EMBR particles with a shared random color
reacts.also: each EMBR gets tmp=1, life 70-109, temp 5750-6249K, inherits half FWRK's velocity plus random spread; local pressure += 8; FWRK destroyed

behaviour: Original fireworks element - self-launches from ambient heat (>400K) in open air, with a small random chance
Also launches immediately if its ctype is set to PT_DUST (e.g. by neutron activation elsewhere)
Detonates into a 40-particle EMBR burst shortly after launch, same visual style as FIRW
Resets to dormant if it somehow reaches life>=45 without detonating
builder_notes: Slower/less reliable ignition than FIRW - depends on temperature and open space, not direct flame contact
The ctype==PT_DUST launch path suggests neutron activation is the more reliable trigger route
Functionally superseded by FIRW for predictable fire-triggered launches

GUNP.name: Gunpowder
behaviour: No custom Update function - all ignition comes from other elements' generic Flammable/Explosive checks (e.g. FIRE.cpp's ignition loop)
Very high Flammable (600) and Explosive=1 make it catch fire easily and add pressure when it burns
Converts directly to FIRE at 673K via the standard engine HighTemperature transition
Powder form falls and piles like sand
builder_notes: Reacts as a highly flammable powder purely through generic fire-spread code, not custom logic in this file
Its Explosive=1 flag causes a pressure kick wherever FIRE's ignition code catches it
673K threshold gives it a slightly lower ignition point than plain heat-only ignition of most materials

IGNT.name: Ignition Cord

props.tmp: 0 = unlit, 1 = lit/burning
props.life: default 3; decremented once lit; each frame while >0, spawns EMBR or FIRE nearby; particle is destroyed (PROP_LIFE_KILL) when life reaches 0

reacts.with: FIRE/PLSM/SPRK/LIGH, or another IGNT with life==1

reacts.result: spawns an EMBR nearby (life 30, heated temp)

behaviour: Chain-ignites along touching IGNT particles that have life==1 (fresh-ignition marker), acting as a burning cord
Converts to FIRE outright at 673K via the standard engine transition
While lit, alternates between throwing off EMBR sparks and small FIRE puffs for exactly `life` frames (default 3)
PROP_SPARKSETTLE lets EMBR rest on it without being destroyed
builder_notes: Short default life (3 frames) means each cord segment burns out fast once lit - chain many segments for a long fuse
Chain-lighting relies on catching the life==1 window of a neighboring IGNT, so propagation speed is roughly one cell per frame
Also detonates plainly at 673K even without a spark, so keep it away from ambient heat if timing matters

LITH.name: Lithium

props.ctype: storedEnergy: li-ion battery charge level (clamped >=0); triggers explosive overcharge around 100
props.tmp: hydrogenationFactor: count of H2-producing reactions absorbed; combined with carbonationFactor it caps further water/CO2 reactions once >=10
props.tmp2: carbonationFactor: count of CO2 molecules absorbed; if <3 when LITH melts it becomes LAVA(LITH), otherwise LAVA(GLAS)
props.life: burnTimer: 0-999 used as a brief post-charge/discharge spark-flare cooldown (set to 8); >=1000 marks active combustion, and hitting exactly 1000 converts LITH to LAVA

reacts.result: spawns a FIRE in the empty cell
neighbor converts to WTRV, neighbor temp set to 440K
neighbor converts to H2; self heats up by 20.365 + storedEnergy^2*1.5, or ignites into full burn (burnTimer=1024+ up to 96) if self already >440K
reacts.also: hydrogenationFactor incremented (or set to 10 if igniting)
reacts.cond: hydrogenationFactor+carbonationFactor<10, not the deep-combustion case above

reacts.result: battery charges: storedEnergy += 1, burnTimer set to 8
reacts.cond: neighbor SPRK's ctype==PSCN, life==3; hydrogenationFactor+carbonationFactor<5; local avg material isn't INSL/RSSS; burnTimer==0

reacts.result: battery discharges: NSCN converts to SPRK (life=4, ctype=NSCN); storedEnergy -= 1, burnTimer set to 8
reacts.cond: neighbor NSCN life==0, storedEnergy>0, burnTimer==0, local avg material isn't INSL/RSSS

reacts.result: both self and O2 neighbor convert to PLSM
reacts.also: local pressure += 4

reacts.result: storedEnergy (charge) equalizes between the two, transferring roughly half the difference; can also propagate a chain-detonation (burnTimer set to 1024) from an already-exploding neighbor
reacts.cond: 9 random samples per frame within radius 3
reacts.chance: up to 9 attempts/frame, first match wins

reacts.result: self converts to LAVA (ctype LITH or GLAS depending on carbonationFactor)
reacts.also: temp set to 500+storedEnergy*10 (LITH) or 2000+storedEnergy*10 (GLAS)
reacts.cond: burnTimer counts exactly down/up to 1000 (from overcharge storedEnergy>=100 or chain-detonation)

behaviour: Extremely multi-functional: reacts with water (produces H2 and heat), CO2 (carbonates), SPRK/NSCN (li-ion battery charge/discharge), FIRE, and O2 (violent PLSM combustion)
Behaves like a battery bank - adjacent LITH particles equalize stored charge and can chain-detonate
Overcharging (storedEnergy>=100) or sustained combustion (burnTimer>=1000) melts it into LAVA, colored by whether it has absorbed enough CO2
Melts to LAVA outright at 453.65K via the standard engine transition as well
builder_notes: Do not let it touch water/DSTW/SLTW/CBNW/WTRV unless H2 production and heat buildup are wanted - it's a real fire hazard
Useful as a distributed rechargeable battery: charge via PSCN spark, discharge into NSCN
Large connected LITH masses can chain-explode once any one particle reaches overcharge or ignition
Pre-carbonating with CO2 changes the final melt product from LAVA(LITH) to LAVA(GLAS)

LRBD.name: Liquid Rubidium
behaviour: No custom Update function - freezes to solid RBDM below 311K and ignites into FIRE above 961K via standard engine transitions
Extremely Flammable (1000) and Explosive=1, so other elements' fire-ignition code treats contact with flame very violently
Conducts electricity like a molten metal
Spawns hot by default (~67C) reflecting its low melting point
builder_notes: Handle like a volatile molten metal - any flame contact (via generic ignition code) is likely to be explosive given Flammable=1000/Explosive=1
Narrow liquid range (311K-961K) - it readily freezes to RBDM or boils to FIRE at moderate temperature swings
No custom water/reaction code in this file, unlike its solid RBDM relative may have

NITR.name: Nitroglycerin
behaviour: Liquid explosive, Explosive=2 (detonates readily), Flammable=1000
No custom update() logic; behaviour is purely property-driven (explosive/flammable engine handles it)
Ignites into FIRE above 673K
Low Hardness (3) and Weight (23), flows like a light liquid
builder_notes: Treat any heat source near 400C+ as a detonation trigger
Pressure/impact-sensitive per Explosive flag - avoid shockwaves nearby
Mixing with CLST (per Description) makes TNT - not verified in this file
Being a liquid, it can seep through gaps solids would block

PLEX.name: C-4
behaviour: Solid pressure-sensitive explosive, Explosive=2
No custom update(); purely property-driven detonation via engine explosive handling
PROP_NEUTPENETRATE: neutrons pass through it without absorbing/scattering
Meltable=50, low Hardness=1 so it's easily destroyed/melted
builder_notes: Safe from neutron-triggered ignition since neutrons pass through it
Still detonates from heat >673K or pressure/impact per Explosive flag
Low hardness means other explosions or impacts crack it easily
Static solid (Gravity=0, Advection=0) - stays exactly where placed until triggered

RBDM.name: Rubidium
behaviour: No custom update() in this file - any water-contact explosion behaviour lives in other elements' files, not verified here
Very low melting point: becomes LRBD (molten) at just 312K (~39C)
PROP_CONDUCTS: carries electrical current like a metal
High HeatConduct=240, conducts heat fast
Explosive=1 and Flammable=1000 per property block
builder_notes: Melts near-room-temperature (39C) - keep away from any warm neighbours
Description warns of water reactivity, but that logic is not in RBDM.cpp itself - verify in WATR.cpp/LRBD.cpp if needed
Conducts current, so treat as a live wire in circuits
Explosive flag means it can be set off by shockwaves/other explosions

THDR.name: Lightning

props.life: Own life not read for behaviour; when THDR converts into FIRE (legacy mode) it seeds the new FIRE particle's life with rng.between(120,169)

reacts.with: any PROP_CONDUCTS element (except WATR/SLTW, target life==0, target ctype!=SPRK)
reacts.also: target.ctype set to its original type; target.life=4; THDR itself is destroyed this tick
reacts.cond: checks all 24 cells in a 5x5 box around self (rx,ry in -2..2, excluding center)

reacts.also: raises pressure in THDR's cell by +100; in legacy mode (sim->legacy_enable) 1/200 chance THDR turns into FIRE (life 120-169) instead of dying

behaviour: Scans a 5x5 area (radius 2) around itself every frame
Turns adjacent conductive, unsparked, non-liquid-water elements into SPRK
Destroys itself on contact with almost anything else, spiking local pressure +100
In legacy mode has a 1/200 chance to become FIRE instead of just dying
Immune interactions: CLNE, itself, SPRK, DMND, FIRE do not destroy it
Extremely hot by default (~9000C) and glows via custom graphics (FIRE_ADD blend)
builder_notes: Use as a one-shot electrifier: touching a wire/conductor sparks it, then THDR self-destructs
Do not expect THDR to persist - it is consumed almost immediately by any non-immune neighbour
Very short-range weapon: 2-cell radius only
Massive local heat pulse (9000C) will ignite/melt anything nearby regardless of the SPRK interaction

THRM.name: Thermite
behaviour: No custom update() function - has no self-contained reactions in THRM.cpp
Description states it burns into molten metal, but that logic must live in FIRE.cpp or similar, not here
Meltable=2 (very easily melted once triggered)
High HeatConduct=211, transfers heat quickly to neighbours
builder_notes: Cannot verify its ignition/burn reaction from this file alone - check FIRE.cpp/PT_LAVA handling
Falls and settles like a powder (Falldown=1, Gravity=0.3)
Conducts heat fast, so a THRM pile heats up together quickly once one particle ignites

ACEL.name: Accelerator

props.tmp: Set to 1 each frame if any neighbour was accelerated this tick (drives PMODE_GLOW in graphics), otherwise reset to 0
props.life: If life!=0, sets the speed multiplier for this tick: 1 + clamp(life,0,1000)/100; life=0 uses a flat default multiplier of 1.1x

behaviour: Every frame, multiplies the velocity of TYPE_PART/LIQUID/GAS/ENERGY particles in its 4 orthogonal neighbour cells (N/S/E/W only, not diagonals)
Also affects PHOT (photon) particles via sim->photons lookup
Default speedup is 1.1x per tick; setting life gives a stronger multiplier up to 2.0x+ (life=1000 caps it)
Resulting velocity is clamped to MAX_VELOCITY while preserving direction
Glows (PMODE_GLOW) whenever it actually sped something up that tick
Static solid, does not move or react chemically itself
builder_notes: Only affects the 4 orthogonally-adjacent cells, not diagonals - orient particle flow accordingly
Set the particle's life value (e.g. via Lua/property tool) to tune acceleration strength beyond the default 1.1x
Stack multiple ACELs along a pipe to compound acceleration cell by cell
Does not affect TYPE_SOLID particles, only moving part/liquid/gas/energy types

DCEL.name: Decelerator

props.tmp: Set to 1 each frame if any neighbour was decelerated this tick (drives PMODE_GLOW in graphics), otherwise reset to 0
props.life: If life!=0 (clamped 0-100), multiplier = 1 - life/100; life=0 uses a flat default multiplier of 1/1.1

behaviour: Every frame, multiplies down the velocity of TYPE_PART/LIQUID/GAS/ENERGY particles in its 4 orthogonal neighbour cells
Also affects PHOT particles via sim->photons lookup
Default slowdown is ~0.91x per tick (1/1.1); life 1-100 can fully stop particles (life=100 -> multiplier 0)
Glows (PMODE_GLOW) whenever it actually slowed something that tick
Static solid, no self-reaction
builder_notes: Only affects orthogonal neighbours (N/S/E/W), not diagonals
Set life close to 100 to nearly stop particles passing by, useful as a velocity gate/filter
Combine with ACEL for speed-control airlocks or particle sorters
Ignores TYPE_SOLID particles entirely

DMG.name: Damage

reacts.with: any element except DMG/EMBR/DMND/CLNE/PCLN/BCLN in its 8 neighbours
reacts.result: DMG self-destructs and triggers a radius-25 blast
reacts.also: kills itself first, then for every particle within a 25-cell radius (Euclidean distance, capped at 25): pushes it outward with a 7.0-magnitude velocity impulse away from the blast centre and adds +1.0 pressure to that particle's cell
reacts.cond: trigger requires touching a non-exempt neighbour; blast covers a huge 51x51 area

reacts.with: any particle in blast radius whose element has a valid HighPressureTransition

reacts.also: result particle's ctype set to PT_TUNG (marks it as a tungsten-derived BRMT)

behaviour: Inert until it touches almost anything (except EMBR, DMND, CLNE/PCLN/BCLN, or another DMG)
On trigger: destroys itself and blasts a 25-cell-radius area with outward force + pressure
Converts many solids in the blast into their 'broken/high-pressure' forms (BRMT, BGLA, BCOL, PQRT, SAWD, or each element's own HighPressureTransition target)
PROP_SPARKSETTLE: settles differently when charged with a spark
High Hardness=20, fairly durable until it triggers
builder_notes: Keep clear of EMBR, DMND, CLNE, PCLN, BCLN if you want to avoid accidental triggering - these are the only safe neighbours
25-cell blast radius is very large; place with wide clearance from anything you don't want shattered
Effective as a wall-breaching/quarrying charge because of its material-transform table
PMODE_FLARE graphics make it glow brightly, useful as a visible fuse-in-waiting indicator

FRAY.name: Force Emitter

props.tmp: Beam length in cells; if tmp>0 that value is used as the ray's max length, otherwise defaults to 10 cells

behaviour: Requires a SPRK particle in one of its 8 neighbour cells to activate
Fires an invisible force beam in the direction opposite the triggering SPRK, up to `tmp` cells long (default 10)
Along the beam, every non-solid particle gets a velocity nudge of coef=(temp-273.15)/10 in the beam direction each frame it's charged
Positive temperature (>273.15K) pushes particles away; negative offset (<273.15K, i.e. below 0C) pulls them toward the emitter
Beam stops early at the simulation edge or after `tmp` steps
Like ARAY but continuous/force-based rather than a drawing ray
builder_notes: Spark it (place SPRK adjacent) every tick you want the force beam active - no spark, no effect
Aim by choosing which side you spark: the beam fires from the opposite side
Set particle temperature below 0C (273.15K) to make it pull/attract instead of push
Set tmp to control beam reach; default reach is only 10 cells
Only affects non-solid particles - walls and solids are unaffected

GBMB.name: Gravity Bomb

props.life: 0 = unarmed/inert; touching any non-exempt neighbour (not BOMB/GBMB/CLNE/PCLN/DMND) arms it by setting life=60; life>20 sets a local gravity 'mass' of +20 (mild pull-in); life 1-20 sets mass=-80 (strong push-out); PROP_LIFE_DEC auto-decrements life each frame, and PROP_LIFE_KILL_DEC destroys the particle once life reaches 0

behaviour: Sticks/arms on first contact with any object except BOMB, GBMB, CLNE, PCLN, DMND
Once armed (life 21-60), generates a weak attractive gravity field (gravIn.mass=20) at its cell
As life decays into the 1-20 range, flips to a strong repulsive gravity field (gravIn.mass=-80) - the 'explosion' phase
Life auto-decays each frame (PROP_LIFE_DEC) and the particle is destroyed at life 0 (PROP_LIFE_KILL_DEC)
Graphics: flares while unarmed (life<=0), sparks while armed/counting down
builder_notes: Behaves like a timed gravity mine: contact arms a ~60-tick fuse before it flips from pulling to pushing
Use the attract phase (life>20) to gather loose particles, then the push phase (life<=20) to scatter them
It self-destroys after the fuse runs out - no need to manually clean it up
Avoid touching it with BOMB/GBMB/CLNE/PCLN/DMND if you want to delay arming

RPEL.name: Repulse

props.ctype: If nonzero, restricts the effect to only particles of that specific type (settable via right-click/CtypeDraw); 0 means it affects all non-solid particles

behaviour: Each frame, samples 11 random cells within a 21x21 area (offsets -10..10) around itself
For each sampled cell containing a non-solid particle matching its ctype filter, nudges that particle's velocity
Force per axis = sign(offset) * (temp-273.15)/10, applied independently to vx and vy
Positive temperature (above 0C) repels matching particles; negative offset (below 0C) attracts them
Random sampling means effect is probabilistic/sparse per tick rather than exhaustive over the whole area
Also affects PHOT particles via the photons map
builder_notes: Set ctype (right-click draw) to target only a specific particle type, or leave 0 to affect everything nearby
Set temperature below 0C to make it an attractor instead of a repeller
Effect is randomized/sparse (only ~11 samples/tick over a 21x21 area), not a uniform field - expect some jitter
Range is much larger (10 cells) than FRAY's beam but omnidirectional and probabilistic rather than a focused beam

BOYL.name: Boyle

reacts.also: self converts to WATR, the O2 particle is killed, and +4.0 pressure is added to the cell

behaviour: Implements Boyle's-law-style pressure: nudges its own cell and all 8 neighbouring cells' pressure toward a target limit = temp/100 each frame (small step, 0.001x the difference)
Hotter BOYL gas drives higher local pressure over time; cooler BOYL relaxes pressure down
Turns adjacent WATR into FOG occasionally (1/30 chance)
Reacts with O2 to form WATR, releasing a burst of pressure (+4.0)
Pure TYPE_GAS with no special flags
builder_notes: Use its temperature as a pressure-control dial - hotter BOYL raises ambient pressure in an enclosed space, cooler lowers it
Effect on pressure is gradual (0.1% step per tick), so give it time to reach steady state
Avoid enclosing BOYL with WATR or O2 nearby if you need a stable pressure source, since both slowly consume/convert it
Good as a slow-acting pneumatic pressure source rather than an instant one

CAUS.name: Caustic Gas

props.life: Acid charge pool, defaults to 75 (DefaultProperties.life). Each successful dissolve costs 1 life while life>50. Once life<=50, it can no longer dissolve targets and instead is destroyed on its next contact with a non-immune neighbour

reacts.result: both CAUS and the GAS neighbour become RFRG
reacts.cond: adjacent within 2 cells, and pressure in the GAS neighbour's cell > 3
reacts.chance: always when condition met (no RNG roll)

reacts.with: any element except ACID/CAUS/RFRG/RFGL (and not CLNE/PCLN; FOG/RIME require target.tmp<=5)
reacts.also: CAUS heats up by newtemp=(60-target.Hardness)*7 (clamped >=0) and loses 1 life; blocked if a GLAS particle sits between CAUS and the target (parts_avg check)
reacts.cond: adjacent within 2 cells, requires CAUS life>50

reacts.with: any non-immune neighbour once CAUS life<=50

behaviour: Acts like ACID per its Description: dissolves most materials on contact, scaled by their Hardness
Starts with a life 'charge' of 75 that depletes with each dissolve; runs out around life<=50
Converts nearby pressurized GAS (pressure>3) into RFRG, turning itself into RFRG too
GLAS acts as a barrier/shield protecting particles behind it from CAUS
PROP_DEADLY: harmful/lethal to creatures per the deadly flag
Self-destructs once its acid charge is spent and it touches something it can't dissolve
builder_notes: Treat as a limited-use acid cloud - it dissolves roughly 12-13 targets (75-50=25 life, costing 1 per hit while >50) before going inert/dying
Shield valuable structures with GLAS to block its dissolving effect
Keep it away from pressurized GAS pockets if you don't want it converted to RFRG
PROP_DEADLY means it will harm any STKM/creature it touches - keep away from playable characters

CO2.name: Carbon Dioxide

props.ctype: ctype==5 marks a CO2 particle formed from BUBW that hasn't yet released its captured water particle; used to conserve total water-particle count and to periodically re-emit a WATR particle into an empty neighbour cell

reacts.also: clears CO2's ctype to 0 (only applies when ctype==5)
1/30 chance CO2 itself is also killed
if CO2's ctype==5, a new WATR particle is created at CO2's own position (water count conserved) and CO2 survives as WATR-source; otherwise CO2 itself is killed (net CO2 consumed)

reacts.result: self converts to O2, plus creates NEUT (and sometimes ELEC)
reacts.also: created NEUT/ELEC temp set to MAX_TEMP; self temp set to MAX_TEMP; +100 pressure added
reacts.chance: 1/5 to trigger, then 1/50 chance to also spawn ELEC

behaviour: Heavier-than-normal gas that drifts downward (Gravity=0.1, Falldown=1)
Freezes into DRIC (dry ice) below 194.65K
Extinguishes FIRE on contact, occasionally being consumed itself
Carbonates WATR/DSTW into CBNW
Under extreme heat+pressure, splits into O2 + NEUT (+ELEC), an unusual fusion/fission-style reaction
ctype=5 marks 'BUBW-origin' CO2 that still owes a WATR particle back to the simulation
builder_notes: Use as a fire suppressant, but expect ~1/30 of your CO2 to be consumed putting out each fire particle
Carbonating water pools slowly converts them to CBNW at 1/50 per adjacent frame - not instant
Cool below -78.5C to solidify into DRIC for CO2 storage/transport
The extreme temp/pressure O2+NEUT reaction only matters near reactor-tier conditions (>9500C, >200 pressure)

FOG.name: Fog

props.ctype: Carries the type of the element it was generated from (CarriesTypeIn = FIELD_CTYPE); cleared to 0 instead of incrementing tmp when it is DSTW and reacts with GAS
props.tmp: Acts as an acidity/reaction counter; increments each time FOG destroys an adjacent GAS particle, gated at tmp<10
props.life: PROP_LIFE_DEC counter; increased by a random 0-19 when touching SPRK; the solid->RIME conversion only happens while life==0

reacts.also: FOG's life increases by a random amount 0-19
reacts.chance: always on contact (no roll for whether it happens, magnitude is randomized)

reacts.also: if FOG.ctype==DSTW, ctype is cleared to 0; otherwise FOG.tmp is incremented (acidity build-up)

behaviour: Cold gas (default -30C) that boils away to WTRV above 100C
Freezes onto solid surfaces into RIME, but only while its life counter is exactly 0
Absorbing a SPRK charges up its life counter, temporarily blocking the RIME conversion
Consumes nearby GAS particles, building up an internal 'acidity' counter (tmp) up to 10
Inherits (carries) the ctype of whatever produced it (e.g. RIME via spark)
builder_notes: Keep FOG away from SPRK if you want it to reliably freeze into RIME on solids
It will happily eat nearby GAS particles until its tmp counter hits 10, then stops
Boils away completely above 100C - not useful in hot environments
High Hardness (30) is irrelevant since it's a gas with no collision solidity; likely just governs frost/rime interactions elsewhere

GAS.name: Gas
behaviour: No custom update() function; all behaviour is property-driven transitions
Liquefies into OIL above 6.0 pressure
Ignites into FIRE above 573K (~300C)
Flammable=600, fairly flammable but no update-based combustion logic here (handled by generic FIRE spread engine)
PROP_NEUTPASS: neutrons pass through without interacting
Diffuses quickly (Diffusion=0.75) and rises with HotAir=0.001
builder_notes: Compress above 6 pressure to convert to OIL - useful for gas-to-liquid storage
Keep below 300C to avoid spontaneous ignition into FIRE
Neutron-transparent, so it won't shield or absorb neutron radiation
Diffuses and spreads fast, hard to contain without solid walls

H2.name: Hydrogen

props.tmp: Bit flags: 0x1 set once this particle has reacted (become FIRE, or undergone fusion into NBLE); 0x4 set on PLSM particles created by H2 fusion, marking them as H2-origin plasma

reacts.result: DESL becomes WATR, H2 becomes OIL
H2 becomes FIRE (creates a FIRE particle)
reacts.also: sets the neighbouring FIRE's temp to 3473K (if tmp&0x02) or 2473.15K otherwise, ORs 0x1 into its tmp; H2's own temp increases by random 0-99
reacts.cond: adjacent within 2 cells, only when cell pressure <= 45.0 (or neighbour temp <= 2273.15 when pressure > 45.0)

reacts.also: H2's temp increases by random 0-99, tmp ORed with 0x1
reacts.cond: adjacent within 2 cells, same pressure gating as FIRE reaction

reacts.also: creates NEUT (temp=own temp); 1/10 chance also creates ELEC (temp=own temp); creates PHOT (ctype=0x7C0000, tmp=0x1, temp=own temp); if a nearby random cell can host PLSM (or is H2), creates a PLSM there (tmp|=4); own temp set to temp+750..1249; cell pressure += 30

behaviour: Highly reactive with FIRE, PLSM, and hot LAVA - turns into FIRE itself on contact (except LAVA with BMTL ctype, which is inert to it)
High pressure (>8) with DESL converts DESL to WATR and H2 to OIL
Under high pressure (>45), it becomes resistant to igniting from neighbours below 2273.15K
Undergoes a fusion-like reaction above 2273.15K and 50 pressure, becoming NBLE while emitting NEUT, PHOT, and sometimes ELEC/PLSM
PROP_PHOTPASS: transparent to photons
Diffuses very fast (Diffusion=3.0) and has zero gravity/weight settling
builder_notes: Extremely fire-prone - any nearby FIRE, PLSM, or non-BMTL LAVA will ignite it
High pressure (>45) can be used as a safety buffer against low-temperature ignition sources
Fusion reactor design: compress H2 above 50 pressure and heat above ~2000C to farm NBLE, NEUT, PHOT, ELEC, and PLSM
Reacts with DESL under moderate pressure (>8) to produce OIL+WATR - useful refinery combo
Photon-transparent, so lasers/photons pass through unaffected

NBLE.name: Noble Gas

props.tmp: Bit flag 0x1 set once this particle has undergone the fusion reaction (marker, not otherwise consumed in this file)

reacts.also: creates NEUT (temp=own temp); 1/25 chance also creates ELEC (temp=own temp); creates PHOT (ctype=0xF800000, tmp=0x1, temp=own temp); if a nearby random cell can host PLSM (or is NBLE), creates a PLSM there (tmp|=4); own temp set to temp+1750+random(0,499); cell pressure += 50

behaviour: Inert diffusing gas under normal conditions (Diffusion=0.75)
Description notes it ionizes into plasma when sparked, but that is handled by the generic PROP_CONDUCTS/SPRK engine, not in NBLE.cpp's own update()
Undergoes a fusion-like reaction above 5273.15K and 100 pressure, converting to CO2 while emitting NEUT, PHOT, and sometimes ELEC/PLSM
Requires notably higher temperature/pressure thresholds than H2's analogous fusion reaction
PROP_CONDUCTS: behaves as an electrical conductor like a metal/gas-discharge tube
builder_notes: Fusion tier is much hotter than H2's (>5000C, >100 pressure) - build accordingly if chaining H2->NBLE->CO2 fusion stages
Conducts electricity - sparking it is handled by the general spark system, not custom logic here
End product of NBLE fusion is CO2, so a two-stage H2->NBLE->CO2 fusion chain is possible under escalating temp/pressure
Low weight/no gravity means it will diffuse and rise/spread rapidly if not contained

O2.name: Oxygen

props.tmp: bit flags set on the resulting FIRE/PLSM particle when O2 ignites (bit0 read from neighbor FIRE, bit1 set on new fire); not a stable property of O2 itself

reacts.also: heats the triggering FIRE by 0-99K, and if that FIRE's tmp bit0 was set, snaps it to 3473K

reacts.cond: within 2 cells, only if neighbor PLSM's tmp bit 0x4 is not set (not already 'spent')

reacts.result: BRMT + NEUT(9999K) + PHOT(9999K) + GRVT(9999K), and sometimes PLSM(9999K) if a neighbor cell can hold it
reacts.also: sets local cell pressure to MAX_PRESSURE and own temp to MAX_TEMP
reacts.cond: own temp > 9973.15K AND local cell pressure > 250 AND local gravity-field vector magnitude^2 > 400

behaviour: Gas that drifts slightly downward (Collision -0.1) with high diffusion (3.0)
Ignites into FIRE on contact with FIRE or fresh PLSM within a 2-cell radius
Freezes into LO2 below 90K
Rare fusion-like burst (needs extreme heat, pressure, and gravity field) spits out BRMT/NEUT/PHOT/GRVT/PLSM
builder_notes: Keep separate from FIRE/PLSM sources unless you want a chain ignition
The 'fusion' reaction is very hard to trigger outside custom-gravity setups
Diffuses fast; don't expect it to pool without containment

PLSM.name: Plasma

props.ctype: carried field (CarriesTypeIn FIELD_CTYPE); if set to PT_NBLE, plasma decays into that noble gas instead of other paths
props.tmp: bit flags: bits 0x1/0x2 track contact with O2/H2 (0x3 together -> becomes steam), bit 0x4 set by O2.cpp to mark plasma that already ignited O2 (prevents re-trigger)
props.life: decay counter, randomized 50-199 on creation; decrements via life_dec; at life<=1 the element checks for decay transitions

reacts.also: life reset to 0

reacts.cond: life <= 1 and both O2/H2 contact bits set

reacts.result: THRM becomes LAVA(ctype=BMTL, temp 3500) or LAVA(ctype=THRM, life 400, temp 3500) plus +50 local pressure

reacts.also: if target is Explosive, local pressure += 0.25*CFDS
reacts.cond: target in open space or Explosive, within 2 cells; excludes some SPRK/PHOT edge cases

behaviour: Ultra-hot gas locked near MAX_TEMP, glows using the plasma color table
Update function is literally shared with FIRE (Element_FIRE_update)
Decays via life counter into WTRV, NBLE, or continues burning
Ignites nearby flammable materials exactly like fire does
builder_notes: Functionally a hotter fire variant for build purposes - respect its ignition radius
Tag ctype=NBLE if you want plasma to fizzle into a specific noble gas
Short-lived unless something keeps regenerating its life value

RFRG.name: Refrigerant

props.tmp: reinterpreted as raw float bits storing the previous frame's local cell pressure; used purely to compute adiabatic-style compression heating, not a normal counter

behaviour: No reactions with other element types; only self-physics
Temperature scales with the ratio of new-to-old local cell pressure each frame (compresses = heats, expands = cools)
Liquefies into RFGL above 2 (pressure-scale) bar
Deadly to stickmen
builder_notes: Use as a compression heater/decompression cooler in pressure-driven machines
Don't manually poke tmp - it's storing a float-encoded pressure value internally
Liquefies at a fairly low pressure threshold (2), so keep pressure below that to keep it gaseous

SMKE.name: Smoke

props.life: decays each frame via life_dec; kills the particle once decremented to <= 0 (life_kill_dec)

behaviour: No update() function at all - purely passive, governed only by property-block physics
Rises (negative gravity), high air drag/loss so it dissipates over time
Reignites into FIRE if reheated above 625K
High heat conduct (88) equalizes temperature with surroundings quickly
builder_notes: Purely decorative/byproduct gas - no direct interactions coded
Can be reignited into fire if a build reheats it above 625K
Will thin out and vanish on its own via the life counter

VRSG.name: Gas Virus

props.tmp2: carried field (CarriesTypeIn FIELD_TMP2); when VRSG infects a particle, that particle's tmp2 is set to its original element type so it can revert after being cured (tmp3/tmp4 also used for cure/lifespan countdowns, not in this schema's 4 slots)

reacts.result: self picks up an increased cure countdown from the neighbor

reacts.also: chance 1/4 to kill the SOAP
reacts.chance: cure add on contact; kill 3/4 chance is NOT killing, i.e. kill happens when rndstore&0x3==0 (~1/4)

reacts.result: self converts to PLSM (virus destroyed by plasma)
reacts.cond: adjacent, target cell has open space (surround_space)

reacts.result: target infected: becomes VRSS if its temp < 305K, VRSG if > 673K, else VIRS
reacts.also: target's original type stored in its tmp2 for later cure reversion

reacts.result: resets own death countdown (tmp4) to 0, effectively making it immortal

behaviour: Shares its update logic with VIRS.cpp (Element_VIRS_update) - hot gaseous phase of the virus
Infects almost anything on contact, converting it to a temperature-appropriate virus variant
DMND and BASE are immune to infection
Self-destructs via a decaying lifespan counter unless refreshed by PROT radiation
Can be cured by SOAP, which also spreads a 'being cured' state to infected neighbors
builder_notes: Very contagious in a 3x3 neighborhood - contain it deliberately
Use SOAP as a virus quarantine/cure tool
High Flammable stat (500) despite being a virus gas - it can be burned away
PROT exposure makes an infection effectively permanent

WTRV.name: Steam

props.ctype: carried field (CarriesTypeIn FIELD_CTYPE); when marked PT_FIRE, triggers a slow passive cooldown above 1273K; also set to PT_WATR when converted into FIRE by RBDM/LRBD

transitions.to: RIME (if colder than 273K) or DSTW (otherwise) - resolved via ST sentinel in core sim

reacts.cond: not legacy mode, own temp > 285.15K, adjacent (8-dir)

reacts.result: temp decreases by temp/1000 each frame

behaviour: Rises (Gravity -0.1); condenses back to liquid below 371K
Below 273K condenses to RIME, otherwise to DSTW (ST sentinel logic)
Can be ignited by reactive metals RBDM/LRBD, like liquid water can
Slowly self-cools when tagged as originating from FIRE, above 1273K
builder_notes: Behaves as water's gas phase; expect quick recondensation below 98C
Watch RBDM/LRBD exposure outside legacy mode - it can spontaneously ignite steam

LIFE.name: Game of Life

props.ctype: selects which GOL ruleset variant this cell belongs to: an index into the builtin GOL table, or a packed custom rule value
props.tmp: packed 'colour2' value for the selected ruleset (used for multi-state color blending)
props.tmp2: number of extra color 'states' for multi-state rulesets, computed as ((ruleset>>17)&0xF)+1

behaviour: Base Game-of-Life element; default Description ruleset is B3/S23 (Conway's classic)
LIFE.cpp itself has no update() function - the actual cellular-automaton stepping (birth/survival) is implemented generically in shared simulation code for any PROP_LIFE element, not in this file
create() maps the given ctype value to a builtin or custom ruleset table entry and derives display colours/state count
MenuVisible=0 - not placed directly from the menu; normally spawned via the GOL tool UI with a chosen ruleset
builder_notes: Different ctype values at placement time produce entirely different cellular automaton rules, not just Conway's Life
This catalog entry cannot describe the birth/survival stepping logic itself since it is not present in LIFE.cpp
Default temp of 9000K appears unused by any transition logic in this file

ACID.name: Acid

props.life: concentration/strength, default 75; each successful dissolve costs 1 life; below life<=50 acid becomes weak and eventually self-destructs; diffuses between adjacent acid particles

reacts.result: both acid and target instantly become FIRE (life=4)
self becomes CAUS (life 25-74), consumes the WTRV
LITH converts to H2; acid survives, loses 1 life, heats up
reacts.also: part of the general dissolve gate below
reacts.cond: adjacent within 2 cells, life > 50, gated by chance(Hardness,1000)

reacts.with: other dissolvable solids/liquids (not CLNE/PCLN, not FOG/RIME unless their tmp<=5)
reacts.result: target destroyed (kill_part) unless GLAS-shielded; acid loses 1 life and heats up by (60-Hardness)*7
reacts.also: GLAS neighbor-average protects the target from dissolving

reacts.cond: life <= 50 and none of the above reactions triggered this neighbor
reacts.chance: every frame while in this state

reacts.cond: within 2 cells, own life greater than neighbor's, own life > 0
reacts.chance: checked twice per frame (2 random samples)

behaviour: Dissolves nearly any solid/liquid based on the target's Hardness stat (softer dissolves faster)
GLAS shielding (via parts_avg with GLAS) protects a target from dissolving
Instantly ignites PLEX/NITR/GUNP/RBDM/LRBD into fire rather than dissolving them
Weakens with each reaction; effectively 'spent' and dying once life drops to 50 or below
Pooled acid equalizes potency with neighboring acid over time (diffusion)
builder_notes: Fresh acid (life=75) is much more corrosive than aged acid (life<=50, nearly inert/dying)
Shield structures from acid with GLAS
Avoid contact with RBDM/LRBD/PLEX/NITR/GUNP if you don't want an instant fire
Acid pools will slowly homogenize their strength via diffusion

BASE.name: Base

props.ctype: set to PT_BASE when frozen into ICEI, marking it for melt-back identification (concentration is not preserved through freezing)
props.tmp: single-frame spark-effect flag, reset to 0 every update and set to 1 when rusting metal or dissolving a hard material (drives the PMODE_SPARK graphic)
props.life: concentration, clamped 1-100, default 76; controls boiling point, freezing point, dilution behaviour, and corrosive strength

reacts.also: otherwise increments life (concentrates) and cools via evaporation enthalpy (-20/life K)
reacts.chance: 1/20, then nested 1/(life+1) to actually boil vs. concentrate

reacts.result: converts to ICEI with ctype=BASE, life reset to 0
reacts.cond: temp < (273.15 - life/4) - freezing point drops as concentration rises

reacts.result: target converts to BASE at a diluted concentration (life/2), splitting the original's concentration
reacts.also: target heats slightly (+saturh/10 K)

reacts.result: mutual life decrement; target becomes SLTW once its life<=50; self becomes SLTW if its own life<=0
reacts.cond: adjacent, target life > 50 and own life > 0 to decrement

reacts.result: mutual life decrement; target killed once its life<=50; self becomes SLTW if its own life<=0
reacts.cond: adjacent, target life > 50 and own life > 0 to decrement

reacts.result: self converts to SOAP, OIL killed

reacts.also: own life--
own life--

reacts.result: self converts to MERC, LAVA killed

reacts.also: own life--, sets own spark flag (tmp=1)
own life -= 2, sets own spark flag (tmp=1)

reacts.cond: within 1 cell, own life greater than neighbor's, own life > 1
reacts.chance: checked twice per frame (2 random samples)

behaviour: Concentration ('life', 1-100) drives boiling point, freezing point, and corrosive strength
Diluted by contact with WATR/DSTW/CBNW, which themselves become BASE at reduced concentration
Neutralizes ACID and CAUS into SLTW
Rusts conductive solids into BMTL with a visible spark effect; corrodes soft materials generally
Explicitly ignores BASE, SALT, SLTW, BOYL, MERC, BMTL, BRMT, SOAP, CLNE, PCLN, and its own frozen forms (BASE.cpp:L114-118)
builder_notes: High concentration (life near 100) corrodes/rusts far faster than dilute base
Concentrated base stays liquid at colder temperatures (freezing point drops with concentration)
Evaporates into BOYL above 120C at low pressure - not stable near open flame at low pressure
Keep away from conductive metal parts you want to preserve

CBNW.name: Carbonated Water

props.ctype: set to 5 when converting into CO2 (used as CO2's carried concentration/ctype value)
props.tmp: fizz/explosion countdown: 0 = calm, >0 means actively fizzing and counting down toward turning into CO2; synchronizes with adjacent CBNW particles
props.tmp2: purely cosmetic carbonation 'speckle' value; drifts toward 20 or randomizes to 0-39 periodically for the graphics function

reacts.result: converts to CO2 (ctype=5), raises local pressure by +0.5
reacts.cond: local cell pressure <= 3 (and either <= -0.5 or a random roll)
reacts.chance: guaranteed if pressure <= -0.5, else 1/4000 per frame

reacts.cond: own fizz countdown tmp has reached 1

reacts.result: synchronizes fizz countdown (tmp) between the two particles

reacts.cond: legacy mode or own temp > 285.15K, adjacent within 1 cell

reacts.also: self also has a chance to be destroyed
reacts.cond: adjacent within 1 cell, FIRE's ctype != PT_WATR

behaviour: Slowly releases CO2 bubbles, faster at low/negative pressure or when touching powders/solids
Fizz state (tmp countdown) synchronizes across adjacent CBNW for a coordinated eruption
Conducts electricity and lets neutrons pass through, unlike DSTW
Extinguishes fire like water, with a small chance of being consumed doing so
builder_notes: Not fully stable even in a sealed calm container - expect gradual CO2 fizzing
Dropping powders/solids into it accelerates gas release
Usable as an electrically-conductive water substitute where DSTW would not conduct

DESL.name: Diesel
behaviour: No update() function - purely governed by the property-block transitions
Explodes into FIRE above 5 (pressure-scale) bar or above 335K (62C)
Mildly flammable (Flammable=2), lower than typical fuels
builder_notes: Sensitive high-temp threshold (62C) - keep away from moderate heat sources
Pressurizing above 5 also ignites it - avoid pressurized diesel tanks near heat

DSTW.name: Distilled Water

For PHOT-contact-triggered decay (2xPHOT), rely on PHOT.cpp's own reaction, not anything in ISOZ.cpp
Cool below 160K to lock it into stable solid ISZS storage

NEUT.name: Neutrons

reacts.also: falls through into ICEI/SNOW case, so also gets moderated (see behaviour)

reacts.also: new neutron inherits 0.25x PLUT's prior velocity + NEUT's velocity; +10*CFDS pressure; FIRE update - THE CHAIN-REACTION FISSION PATH
reacts.chance: outer: (3+pressure)/1000; then 2/3 of those hits go this branch

reacts.chance: 1/10 pick of which field to mutate, then always flips one bit

behaviour: Weightless energy particle flying in a straight line until its life counter (480-959 ticks) expires.
Moderated (velocity x0.995/frame) by WATR, ICEI, or SNOW contact - the classic reactor moderator materials.
PLUT is the only true chain-reaction fuel here: each adjacent PLUT has a (3+pressure)/1000 chance/frame to react, 2/3 of the time spawning an ADDITIONAL neutron (fission multiplication).
The other 1/3 of PLUT reactions instead transmute it into URAN or molten LAVA(PLUT) at MAX_TEMP and add +10*CFDS pressure.
DEUT neighbors can erupt into up to 340 new NEUT at once (fusion-like DeutExplosion), scaled by DEUT's own life and local pressure.
URAN is NOT referenced anywhere in this file - unlike PLUT, uranium does not absorb, fission, or multiply neutrons here.
TTAN reliably absorbs stray neutrons (1/20 chance, kills the neutron) - useful as a shielding/moderator-adjacent material.
Stray neutrons also "activate" many fuels/organics in passing (COAL/BCOL/PLNT->WOOD/SAWD, DUST->FWRK, ACID->ISOZ, GUNP->DUST) even far from a reactor core.
builder_notes: Use PLUT, not URAN, as the multiplying fuel for a self-sustaining chain reaction - URAN only self-heats under pressure.
Surround a reactor core with WATR/ICEI/SNOW to moderate (slow) neutrons rather than let them fly through unaffected.
TTAN makes an effective neutron absorber/shield (1/20 kill chance per contact).
Watch for side reactions: neutrons leaking out of a core will quietly convert nearby DUST/COAL/ACID/GUNP into other materials.
Each PLUT+NEUT fission event adds pressure (+10*CFDS) - expect pressure buildup and a self-reinforcing feedback loop in confined cores.

PHOT.name: Photons

props.life: default 680, decremented every frame (PROP_LIFE_DEC/LIFE_KILL_DEC); QRTZ/PQRT increments it each pass to delay death

Above 506K, has a 1/10 chance per frame to ignite flammable materials via FIRE update logic (src PHOT.cpp:L67-69).
ISOZ/ISZS act as a gain medium: 1/400 chance to spawn an extra photon while draining 15*CFDS of local pressure.
QRTZ/PQRT filter white light down to one narrow colour band and extend the photon's remaining life.
BGLA refracts the photon path by a small random angle, simulating glass refraction.
RSST (wet resin/concrete) solidifies into its recorded ctype target when struck by a photon, consuming the photon (laser curing).
builder_notes: Use ISOZ/ISZS chains to build simple laser amplifiers (each pass has a small chance to add a photon).
QRTZ is a practical way to convert a white beam into a single-colour beam for filter-based logic.
RSST can be selectively cured/solidified with aimed photon pulses rather than mass NEUT exposure.
Photon lifetime is finite (680 ticks default) - long light-guides need periodic reinforcement or QRTZ life-extension.

PLUT.name: Plutonium

reacts.also: self converts in place into a NEUT particle - passive spontaneous-fission neutron source
reacts.cond: cell pressure must be positive (int(5*pressure) used as chance numerator)

behaviour: The only true fissile/chain-reaction fuel among these elements (see NEUT.cpp's dedicated PLUT case: 2/3 chance to emit an extra NEUT, 1/3 chance to melt into URAN or LAVA(PLUT) at MAX_TEMP when struck by a neutron).
Also passively self-converts into a bare NEUT particle when under positive local pressure (chance scales with pressure), independent of any neutron strike.
PROP_NEUTPASS means it does not absorb/reflect neutrons by default flag - NEUT.cpp's explicit case override is what makes it react.
Heavy powder (weight 90, Falldown=1) that piles like sand/gunpowder.
Has no self temperature or pressure phase transition of its own; it only changes state via nuclear reactions.
builder_notes: Pressurize a PLUT pile to get spontaneous neutron emission even without an external NEUT source.
Combine PLUT with a NEUT source plus confinement (to trap the +10*CFDS pressure added per fission event) to build a runaway chain reaction.
Fissioning PLUT melts into LAVA(PLUT) at MAX_TEMP - expect it to ignite/melt anything nearby.
PLUT will not react with heat, chemicals, or most other elements directly - only neutrons and pressure trigger it.

POLO.name: Polonium

props.tmp: counts neutron-emission events so far; emission is only allowed while tmp < LIMIT (5); at tmp>=LIMIT the particle is "spent" and renders gray instead of glowing
props.tmp2: counts absorbed PROT hits; at tmp2>=10 the POLO transmutes into PLUT (proton-breeding path)
props.life: cooldown timer set to COOLDOWN (15) immediately after each neutron emission; PROP_LIFE_DEC ticks it to 0, after which another emission becomes possible

reacts.also: starts life=COOLDOWN(15), tmp++; self temp becomes ((self.temp+new NEUT.temp)+600)/2 and is copied to the new neutron - only fires from the pristine state (tmp==0)
reacts.cond: life==0 and tmp<LIMIT(5) and tmp==0 (first emission only)

reacts.with: any energy particle overlapping the same cell (checked via sim->photons layer)

reacts.cond: life==0 and tmp<LIMIT(5) and something occupies the energy layer on this cell

reacts.also: increments tmp2 (proton-absorption counter); kills the PROT
reacts.cond: PROT occupies the energy layer on this cell

reacts.also: self temp becomes (temp+600)/2

behaviour: Spontaneously emits one NEUT (1/10000 chance) only from its pristine state (tmp==0); each emission starts a 15-tick cooldown.
Any energy particle (photon/proton/electron/neutron) sharing its cell gives a 1/100 chance/frame to emit another NEUT, up to LIMIT=5 total emissions.
Once tmp reaches 5 it goes visually "spent" (renders solid gray instead of glowing) and stops emitting neutrons.
Absorbing 10 PROT hits (tmp2>=10) breeds the POLO into PLUT, restarting its nuclear potential as true fissile fuel.
Continuously self-heats toward its 388.15K baseline (+0.2K/frame) whenever below that temperature - always stays warm.
Melts into LAVA(POLO) at 526.95K (HighTemperature transition).
PROP_DEADLY makes it lethal to stickmen regardless of its emission state.
Each neutron emission event runs hot (mixes in a +600K bonus), so POLO-seeded neutrons start out very energetic.
builder_notes: Use POLO as a weak, self-limiting neutron starter charge (max 5 emissions) rather than a sustained source.
Bombard spent POLO with a PROT beam (10 hits) to breed it into PLUT for a real chain-reaction fuel.
Keep stickmen away from POLO builds entirely - it's deadly by contact independent of any nuclear activity.
Expect POLO to liquefy into radioactive LAVA(POLO) if a reactor's local heat exceeds 526.95K.

PROT.name: Protons

props.tmp: accumulated collision energy (sum of squared velocities) gained from head-on collisions with another PROT; once past a threshold it transmutes the proton into a heavier element on the next update (NBLE/CO2/O2/PLSM/POLO/URAN/PLUT/SING/AMTR ladder)
props.life: DefaultProperties.life=75, but create() overrides it to 680 when hand-placed; decremented only while sitting in a vacuum (PT_NONE underneath) - does NOT decay while embedded in matter; reaching 0 in vacuum kills it

reacts.also: reverts the spark back to its original (ctype) element with a life boost of 44+life; if the revert fails, resets that particle's life/ctype instead

reacts.result: n x PROT (n=DEUT.life/50, clamped 1-340) via DeutImplosion
reacts.also: kills the DEUT; new protons spawn at temp = DEUT.temp + DEUT.life*500 (clamped); pressure -= 6*CFDS*n (implosion, opposite sign of NEUT's DeutExplosion)
self converts to PHOT, life doubled, ctype reset to full spectrum (0x3FFFFFFF)
sets EXOT.ctype = PT_PROT (tags it)
adjusts WIFI.temp based on PROT's own temp band (very cold PROT: -1000; cold: -100; hot: +1000; warm: +100) - used as a signal probe
kills both the RSSS and the proton itself

adds heat proportional to that material's Flammable*5; adds +1.0 pressure

reacts.result: tmp added to the other proton; self killed

reacts.cond: another PROT occupies the cell directly ahead

same spawn/kill mechanics

behaviour: Does NOT decay via PROP_LIFE_DEC - its life counter only ticks down (and can kill it) while traveling through vacuum (PT_NONE); it is effectively immortal while embedded in matter.
Two protons colliding nearly head-on (within a narrow ~180-degree window, combined v^2>10) merge into one proton carrying the summed kinetic energy as tmp.
Accumulated tmp above threshold transmutes the proton into a heavier element on the next tick: NBLE -> CO2 -> O2 -> PLSM -> POLO -> URAN -> PLUT -> SING (or AMTR if on TUNG) in ascending tmp order.
tmp > 500000 spawns a SING (singularity/black hole) unless the proton is sitting on TUNG, which yields the safer AMTR instead.
Drags any material it touches toward its own temperature by 1/4 per frame every frame - functions as a directed heating beam.
Erases active SPRK back to the underlying conductor, adding a life boost - a proton beam can "reset" wiring.
Ignites flammable/explosive material (including BANG) once its own temperature exceeds 773.15K.
Punches through and destroys RSSS (wet cement), killing itself in the process; converts LCRY-amplified beams into PHOT.
builder_notes: To manufacture URAN/PLUT/POLO deliberately, fire two proton beams at each other so they collide nearly head-on with enough combined speed.
Route an over-energized proton beam through TUNG to get AMTR instead of a SING - much safer output at extreme tmp.
Guard against accidental SING formation: sufficiently energetic proton pileups will eventually spawn one.
Because PROT only decays in vacuum, protons trapped inside solid structures persist indefinitely until they collide or transmute.
Use RSSS as a sacrificial proton sink/decommissioning wall - it destroys both itself and the proton.

SING.name: Singularity

props.tmp: captured-mass counter; incremented by +3 per normal particle absorbed (merging with another SING instead adds that SING's full life); its magnitude on death drives the pop's spawn count and the pressure dumped into surrounding cells
props.life: mass/charge, randomized 60-109 at creation, decremented every frame (PROP_LIFE_DEC); -life is the target pressure it pulls its cell and neighbors toward; growth is capped at 255; the particle pops when life<1

reacts.also: self.life += 3 and tmp++ (absorbing it), or if a merge would exceed life 255 there is instead a 1/1000 chance to convert the target into a brand-new SING (life 60-109); temperature is averaged in and the target is killed either way
reacts.chance: 1/3 to attempt per neighbor per frame

reacts.also: merges: self.life += neighbor.life (skipped this frame if the sum would exceed 255); neighbor killed
reacts.chance: 1/3 to attempt per neighbor per frame

reacts.also: spawncount scales with |tmp| (up to ~3019 particles when |tmp|>255); each spawned particle gets random life (0-299), temp=MAX_TEMP/2, and random velocity up to 5; also dumps tmp as pressure into the surrounding 3x3 block of cells; kills itself

behaviour: Generates strong negative pressure in itself and neighboring/diagonal cells proportional to -life ("suction" scales with mass).
Life (60-109 at creation) is a decaying mass counter (PROP_LIFE_DEC) that also sets suction strength.
Absorbs roughly 1/3 of adjacent particles per frame - except DMND, which is completely immune to absorption.
Each absorption grows life by 3 and increments tmp (a captured-mass tally); two adjacent SING (life>10 each) merge into one, capped at life 255.
If growth would exceed the life-255 cap, there's a 1/1000 chance to instead convert the neighbor into an entirely new SING rather than absorbing it.
When life decays to 0 it "pops": dumps its captured pressure across a 3x3 block and detonates into a shower of PHOT/NEUT/ELEC scaled by captured tmp.
A heavily-fed SING (large tmp) produces a much more violent pop - up to ~3019 spawned particles.
builder_notes: Contain a SING with DMND walls - it is the only material it cannot eat through.
Every SING eventually dies from life decay and detonates; plan for the blast radius (3x3 pressure spike plus a large particle spray).
Feeding a SING past its life-255 growth cap risks it budding an uncontrolled second singularity instead of just growing.
Merging two adjacent SING (both life>10) is a way to consolidate multiple singularities into one, up to life 255.

URAN.name: Uranium
behaviour: Has no reaction to neutrons or any other element in its own file - it is purely a heat-under-pressure passive fuel here.
Self-heating feedback loop: under positive local cell pressure, its temperature compounds by a factor of (1+pressure/2000) every frame (runaway heating when confined).
This self-heating is only active in non-legacy simulation mode (sim->legacy_enable == false).
Falls/piles as a heavy powder (weight 90, Falldown=1); temperature is clamped to [MIN_TEMP, MAX_TEMP].
Contrast with PLUT (see NEUT.cpp): PLUT is the actual chain-reaction fuel that multiplies neutrons; URAN neither emits nor absorbs NEUT and does not fission.
builder_notes: Pressurize/confine URAN piles to trigger runaway self-heating - good for slow "decay heat" effects, not for neutron-driven chain reactions.
URAN will not multiply neutrons or sustain a fission chain - use PLUT for that purpose instead.
The self-heating loop has no cap besides MAX_TEMP - sustained pressure can drive a pile to maximum temperature over time.
URAN's self-heating is disabled entirely if the simulation is run in legacy heat mode.

VIBR.name: Vibranium

props.tmp: stored thermal/pressure energy currency; grows from absorbing excess heat (>274.65K) or pressure (>2.5), is discharged as heat (x3) into a random neighbor before detonation, and triggers a 750-tick fuse (life=750) once it exceeds 1000; clamped to [0, 32768] every frame
props.tmp2: detonation-outcome flag: 0 at the final tick (life==1) means the normal EXOT+ELEC+PHOT+BREC explosion happens; a nonzero value (set by a dud-signal from a neighboring exploding VIBR, or by CFLM contact) makes it fizzle back to baseline instead
props.life: 0 = calm/absorbing state; set to 750 to begin the detonation countdown (decremented via PROP_LIFE_DEC); sparks arc into conductive neighbors while life<300, heat is dumped into a random neighbor while life<500, and the final detonation/fizzle decision happens at life==1

reacts.also: local pressure -= 1

reacts.cond: adjacent (8-dir), self is exploding (life>0), neighbor is calm (life==0)

reacts.also: sets the neighbor's tmp2=1 (marks it to fizzle) and resets self.tmp=0

reacts.with: PROP_CONDUCTS element (not BREC, not already sparked)
reacts.also: gives it life=4 and ctype = its own original type before sparking
reacts.cond: one random orbit neighbor sampled per frame, only while life<300 and exploding
reacts.chance: sampled once per frame (not probabilistic beyond the sample)

reacts.with: a random nearby cell (any non-VIBR/BVBR, non-heat-insulator)
reacts.also: dumps tmp*3 heat into it and resets self.tmp to 0
reacts.cond: sampled once per frame, only while life<500 and exploding

reacts.also: spawned ELEC/PHOT/BREC all set to 7000K; self becomes EXOT at 9000K with tmp2=random(0,999); local pressure += 50
equalizes tmp between the two (transfers half the difference toward the lower one) - spreads stored energy across a network
reacts.cond: up to 9 randomized nearby-cell samples per frame, first VIBR/BVBR match wins

behaviour: Passively absorbs excess heat (>274.65K, cooling itself by 3K) and pressure (>2.5, draining 1 unit) into an internal tmp energy store.
Also draws on stored tmp to warm itself when very cold (<271.65K) or to counter negative pressure (<-2.5).
Once tmp exceeds 1000, starts a 750-tick detonation countdown (life=750).
During the last 300 ticks it arcs sparks into a random adjacent conductor; during the last 500 ticks it dumps 3x its tmp as heat into a random nearby cell.
At the final tick it normally erupts into EXOT (9000K) plus ELEC/PHOT/BREC shrapnel and adds +50 pressure - unless flagged to fizzle instead (resets to 273.15K quietly).
An exploding VIBR pushes +45 tmp into calm neighboring VIBR/BVBR, propagating a chain detonation across a connected network.
Shares its tmp energy currency with neighboring VIBR/BVBR each frame (like heat diffusion), evening out charge across a network.
Touching ANAR permanently converts it to BVBR; touching EXOT while calm has a 1/25 chance of melting straight into EXOT, skipping the fuse entirely.
builder_notes: Vibranium networks share stored energy - one overloaded cell can trigger a cascading chain of detonations, not just a single explosion.
CFLM (cold flame) can defuse an already-triggered VIBR before its final tick.
BREC neighbors are specifically excluded from being sparked by an exploding VIBR.
Feeding steady heat/pressure into a VIBR is a reliable way to trigger a timed 750-tick fuse rather than an instant blast.
The final blast yields very-high-temperature EXOT, ELEC, PHOT, and BREC - shield sensitive equipment nearby.

WARP.name: Warp

props.tmp2: energy counter (not set anywhere in this file, presumably driven externally e.g. by scripts/other elements); above 2000 makes WARP superheat to 10000K, raise local pressure, and occasionally emit ELEC
props.life: randomized 70-164 at creation, decremented via PROP_LIFE_DEC, destroys the particle at 0 (PROP_LIFE_KILL); each successful displacement of another particle adds +4

reacts.also: sets own temp=10000, raises local pressure by (tmp2/5000)*CFDS, and 1/50 chance to spawn an ELEC particle
reacts.chance: condition check every frame; ELEC spawn at 1/50

reacts.also: directly swaps positions with the target (teleport-style displacement, not physics push); target receives a randomized velocity; self.life += 4
reacts.cond: random adjacent cell sampled, up to 5 attempts per frame, stops after first successful swap
reacts.chance: certain once a valid, non-immune target is sampled

behaviour: Displaces (teleports) whatever it touches by directly swapping positions rather than pushing via normal physics.
Immune to displacement: itself, STKM/STKM2 (stickmen), DMND, and the CLNE/BCLN/PCLN clone family.
Each successful displacement extends its own life by +4 ticks.
Life (70-164 at creation) decays every frame and the particle is destroyed at 0 (PROP_LIFE_KILL).
If tmp2 exceeds 2000 it becomes superheated (10000K), raises local pressure, and has a 1/50 chance per frame to emit ELEC.
Renders fully transparent (colour/alpha forced to 0, NO_DECO) - not visually obvious in the sim view.
builder_notes: Don't rely on WARP to relocate stickmen, DMND, or clone-family elements - it ignores/passes them by.
WARP is invisible on screen; an active one wandering through a build can silently scramble layouts.
If something external drives tmp2 above 2000, WARP becomes a stealth heat and ELEC source.
Because life extends on every successful teleport, an actively-displacing WARP in a busy area can far outlast its base 70-164 tick lifespan.

BCOL.name: Broken Coal

props.tmp: unused by BCOL's own behaviour (the tmp-adjustment branch in the shared COAL update only runs when part type==PT_COAL, which BCOL never is)
props.tmp2: tracks the highest temperature reached; used only to tint the ember/glow graphics
props.life: default 110; once below 100 it decrements every frame and spawns a nearby FIRE particle each tick; reaching 0 converts the particle itself into FIRE

behaviour: Shares its update/graphics functions with COAL (Element_COAL_update/graphics, defined in COAL.cpp:L52-76).
Life (default 110) ticks down once below 100, spawning a nearby FIRE particle every tick - it smolders/burns slowly.
When life reaches 0, the BCOL particle itself converts to FIRE.
Unlike plain COAL, BCOL never regenerates or converts back to COAL - its tmp-based pressure/cooling logic is inert for this type.
Records peak temperature (tmp2) purely for a heat-glow colour effect.
builder_notes: Treat BCOL as coal that's already burning down - its life counter guarantees eventual ignition once below 100.
Good as a slow-burning fuel source, but not reusable/rechargeable the way COAL's pressure mechanic allows.

BGLA.name: Broken Glass
behaviour: Has no custom update function at all - pure generic physics and heat transfer, no coded reactions with other elements.
Both neutrons and photons pass straight through it (PROP_NEUTPASS, PROP_PHOTPASS) - transparent to both radiation types.
PROP_DEADLY: lethal to stickmen on contact.
Glows when hot (PROP_HOT_GLOW) and melts to LAVA(GLAS) at 1973K.
Meltable=5 (fairly meltable relative to other broken-solid powders).
builder_notes: Good as a NEUT/PHOT-transparent radiation window or shielding gap since it neither blocks nor absorbs either.
Keep away from stickmen - deadly by touch even without melting.
Formed elsewhere from glass breaking under pressure; will re-melt into lava-glass under sustained extreme heat.

BREC.name: Broken Electronics

props.life: acts as a charge gate; the pressure-heating/EXOT-conversion logic only runs while life is nonzero (e.g. after being sparked); decremented via PROP_LIFE_DEC

reacts.also: sets life=1000 on conversion

behaviour: Must have nonzero life (i.e., recently charged/sparked) for any of its update logic to run.
While charged and local pressure > 10, self-heats by pressure/8 every frame.
If simultaneously very hot (>9000K) and under high pressure (>30) while charged, has a 1/200 chance per frame to become EXOT.
Conducts electricity (PROP_CONDUCTS) despite being "broken" and glows when hot (PROP_HOT_GLOW).
builder_notes: Spark BREC first to give it charge (life) before expecting any heating or EXOT-conversion behaviour.
Combine sparking + high pressure (>30) + extreme heat (>9000K) to farm EXOT from broken electronics.

BRMT.name: Broken Metal

props.ctype: carries the original metal's type (CarriesTypeIn = FIELD_CTYPE) so the resulting LAVA melt knows which metal it came from
props.life: not read anywhere in BRMT's own update(); still decremented by PROP_LIFE_DEC but has no effect on BRMT's coded behaviour

reacts.result: THRM (either the BREC neighbor or the BRMT itself, 50/50)
reacts.chance: 1/tempFactor, where tempFactor = max(2, 1000-((523.15-temp)*2)) - i.e. rises toward 1/2 as temperature climbs
