Above 523.15K (250C), reacts with adjacent BREC to form THRM (thermite); reaction odds rise with temperature, capping near 1/2 chance per frame.
Either the BRMT or the touched BREC becomes THRM (50/50 split), never both at once from a single trigger.
Melts via the special ST ctype-aware transition into the matching metal's LAVA at 1273K.
builder_notes: Keep BRMT away from BREC above 250C unless spontaneous THRM formation is desired.
Preserve BRMT's ctype field when copying/relocating it so it melts into the correct metal's lava.

CLST.name: Clay Dust

props.tmp: random speckle value (0-6) assigned at creation, used only for graphics texture

reacts.also: kills the WATR neighbor
nudges velocity toward the neighbor (cohesion), strength 0.05 (<195K), 0.015 (<295K), 0.01 (<350K), else 0.005

Converts to PSTS (paste) on contact with WATR at a low chance (1/1500) checked over a 5x5 neighborhood.
Instantly detonates into BANG on contact with NITR (nitroglycerin) - no chance gate needed.
Melts to LAVA(CLST) at 1256K.
builder_notes: Never store CLST next to NITR - contact alone guarantees an explosion.
Use CLST + WATR (slow, low-probability) to manufacture PSTS/paste over time.
Cold CLST piles compact/clump faster due to stronger low-temperature cohesion.

CNCT.name: Concrete
behaviour: No custom update function - relies purely on generic physics/stacking (per its description, it can stack on itself or ROCK).
Glows when hot (PROP_HOT_GLOW).
Melts to LAVA(CNCT) at 1123K.
builder_notes: Reliable structural powder with no coded surprise reactions - safe as a general filler/structure material.
Will melt if exposed to sustained heat above 1123K (e.g. nearby lava or reactor overheat).

DUST.name: Dust
behaviour: No custom update function - relies purely on generic physics and the Flammable=10 field for standard fire-spread.
Very light powder (weight 85) that is flammable.
High hardness (30) despite being a light powder.
Explicitly disables custom graphics (Graphics=nullptr in its own definition).

It only reacts via OTHER elements' code (e.g. NEUT converts DUST into FWRK) - nothing is coded in DUST.cpp itself.

DYST.name: Dead Yeast
behaviour: Hidden from the element menu (MenuVisible=0) - only appears as a byproduct of other elements' reactions (e.g. NEUT irradiating YEST, per NEUT.cpp).
No custom update function of its own.
More flammable than plain DUST (Flammable=20 vs 10).
Burns down into plain DUST at 473K (200C).

Handle it as a more combustion-prone material than DUST once it forms.

FRZZ.name: Freeze Powder

reacts.also: gives the converted WATR life=100; kills the FRZZ particle itself (consumed)

behaviour: Converts adjacent WATR into FRZW (1/20 chance per frame per neighbor), consuming itself in the process - spreads freezing outward one particle at a time.
Turns to SNOW under pressure > 1.8, to ICEI below 50K, and melts to FRZW (not plain WATR) above 273.15K.
Defaults to a cold -20C (253.15K) starting temperature.
builder_notes: One FRZZ particle can seed a freezing chain reaction through a body of WATR, converting many particles before it's consumed.
Keep local pressure below 1.8 to prevent FRZZ from turning into SNOW instead.
Melting FRZZ yields FRZW (reactive frozen water), not plain WATR - check FRZW's own behaviour for downstream effects.

PQRT.name: Powdered Quartz

props.tmp: Growth charge counter, incremented by absorbing adjacent SLTW; when >0 (and stationary) enables spawning/growing into QRTZ crystal (shared QRTZ.cpp update code). Special QRTZ-only stress check that produces PQRT from QRTZ is skipped for PQRT itself (guarded by type==PT_QRTZ).

props.life: Growth-lock timer, clamped to <=5; blocks further growth/diffusion attempts while >0 (set to 5 right after the QRTZ->PQRT conversion, not reachable directly from PQRT's own code).

reacts.also: SLTW killed, PQRT.tmp += 1
self (the PQRT particle) converts to QRTZ; own tmp--; new QRTZ born 'dead' (tmp=-1) 50% of the time
reacts.cond: tmp>0, velocity^2<0.2, life<=0; tries up to 9 random offsets (within ~2px) per frame looking for an empty cell
reacts.chance: deterministic once conditions/empty cell found, up to 9 tries/frame

behaviour: Broken/powder form of QRTZ; photons pass through it and it hot-glows when heated
Absorbs adjacent SLTW (1/500/frame), banking growth charge in tmp

Very heat-resistant, only melts to lava at 2573.15K
builder_notes: A resting PQRT pile is not static - it will slowly regrow into QRTZ crystal over time if tmp>0
Keep pure PQRT deposits away from SLTW if you don't want it accumulating growth charge
Safe near almost all hot builds given its 2573K melting point

SALT.name: Salt
behaviour: No update() function at all - purely a passive powder in its own source file

Meltable=5, Hardness=1 - soft and can shock-melt on high-velocity impact

Relatively low melting point; keep clear of lava/molten-metal builds

SAND.name: Sand
behaviour: No update() function - pure physical powder, no coded reactions in this file

Meltable=5, Hardness=1
Melts to lava at 1973K
builder_notes: Used as a growth substrate for SEED (per SEED.cpp), but SAND.cpp itself has no awareness of that
High melting point makes it a decent heat-tolerant fill material

SAWD.name: Sawdust
behaviour: No update() function and Graphics explicitly set to nullptr - a minimal, purely physical powder
No HighTemperature transition field (ITH/NT) - never melts/boils via the standard transition system
Very light (Weight=18) with low Gravity(0.1)/high Advection(0.7) so it floats on water and drifts in air
Flammable=10; burning is handled entirely by the generic fire-propagation engine, not by SAWD's own code
Neutrons pass straight through
builder_notes: Good floating decorative/fuel powder - expect it to ride currents and sit on liquids
No custom code here to reference for advanced interactions

SEED.name: Seed

props.ctype: Bit-packed genetics shared with PLNT's layout (PLNT_DIR/PLNT_PHASE/PLNT_COLOUR bit-fields). Bit 0 doubles as a 'has already bred' lock. Bits at PLNT_LIFE (top byte) store the absorbed water amount (0-255).

props.tmp3: Same role as tmp (branch-pattern genetics bits).
props.tmp4: Same role as tmp (branch-pattern genetics bits, PLNT_TOTAL_TMP bits total).

transitions.when: temp_high_and_pressure_high (custom code, not the HighTemperature field)

reacts.also: sets PLNT direction/phase ctype bits, life = 15*water for first branch length
reacts.cond: water>3 stored, empty cell above the seed, life counter exceeds 200 while continuously resting on the support

reacts.also: WATR killed, water += 1, life reset to 0
reacts.chance: every frame while condition holds (no extra rng roll)

reacts.also: DEUT killed, water += 1, life reset to 0
particle killed, water += 1, life reset to 0
SLTW killed, water -= 1, life reset to 0
SPNG.life -= 1, water += 1, life reset to 0
genetic crossover of ctype colour-genes and tmp-tmp4 branch bits between both seeds; both ctype bit0 set to lock further breeding
reacts.cond: adjacent (8-dir), water>0, neither seed already bred

behaviour: Germinates into PLNT after resting >200 frames on SAND/SPNG with water>3 and headroom above
Drinks WATR/DEUT/CBNW/DSTW (different absorption caps), harmed by adjacent SLTW
Can siphon water from a charged SPNG
Two un-bred adjacent seeds breed (1/10 chance), mixing colour and branch-shape genetics
Liquefies into MWAX under heat+pressure (>320K, >50 pressure, 1/150/frame)
Ignites into FIRE above 673.15K; loses stored water/growth progress outside 278.15-343.15K
builder_notes: Plant farms need a SAND or SPNG base plus open space directly above the seed
Keep SLTW away from seed beds - it actively drains their water reserve
Touching seeds will randomly cross-breed; isolate stock if controlled traits matter
Avoid warm (>320K), pressurized (>50) seed piles - they turn to wax instead of growing

SLCN.name: Powdered Silicon

props.ctype: Set to PT_SLCN when the particle converts to SPRK, so it can revert to SLCN correctly afterward.
props.tmp: Bit-packed sparkle animation state: bits 0-11 phase, bits 12-15 current palette index, bits 16-19 next palette index, bits 20-31 phase increment. Zero also acts as an 'uninitialized' sentinel that triggers re-seeding via initSparkles(). Purely cosmetic (drives graphics()).
props.life: 0 normally; set to 4 when the particle conducts a spark relayed from a nearby low-life SPRK.

reacts.also: life set to 4, ctype set to PT_SLCN
reacts.cond: own life==0, own temp<373.15K, SPRK found at one of 4 orthogonal probe points 4px away

behaviour: Conducts electricity, with an extra custom long-range (4px orthogonal) spark-relay check beyond normal wire adjacency
Life-decrements automatically once sparked (PROP_LIFE_DEC)
Continuously cycles through a 16-colour speckle palette purely for visual texture
Occasionally flares/sparkles visually (~1/887 and ~1/593 chance per frame) - cosmetic only
Melts to lava at a very high 3538.15K

The tmp field is animation noise/state - don't read it as meaningful simulation data

SNOW.name: Snow

props.ctype: If equal to PT_FRZW, the snow keeps cooling by 1K/frame. CarriesTypeIn (FIELD_CTYPE) is set on the element, so ctype is preserved from whatever created it (e.g. ICE breaking under pressure).

transitions.to: ST (special transition - target resolved by extra engine code, not a plain element)

behaviour: Default spawn temperature is colder than room temp (265.15K, R_TEMP-30)
If tagged with ctype==FRZW it keeps self-cooling by 1K every frame
Dissolves adjacent SALT/SLTW into SLTW at a 1/333 chance, itself becoming SLTW too
Melts (via special transition) above 252.05K; description notes it's produced when ICE breaks under pressure (that logic lives in ICE.cpp, not verified here)
builder_notes: Don't stack SNOW against SALT if you want a clean crystal - it will slowly wet it into brine
Melts well below 0C game-temp equivalent (252.05K) - it is not very cold-hardy relative to ICE

STNE.name: Stone
behaviour: No update() function - purely physical, no coded reactions in this file
Meltable=5, Hardness=1 (relatively soft/breakable, per Element.h semantics)
Melts to lava at 983K - the lowest melting point of the powders covered here
builder_notes: Cheapest-to-melt heavy powder in this set - avoid placing near lava/hot metal if you want it to stay solid
Frequently the byproduct of other elements breaking (e.g. BRCK under pressure), per those elements' own files

YEST.name: Yeast

reacts.result: spawns a new YEST particle at a random +/-1px offset
reacts.also: self is not consumed; this is self-replication
reacts.chance: every frame within that temperature band (no probability roll)

behaviour: Self-replicates every frame while warm (303K-317K), spawning a new YEST particle adjacent to itself
Gets 'infected' into DYST by adjacent DYST particles (1/6/frame, non-legacy mode only)
Flammable (15); turns into DYST (not fire) at 373K via the standard high-temp transition
builder_notes: Warm yeast piles grow exponentially - watch particle-count budgets, this can flood a sim fast
One DYST particle touching a YEST colony will convert it over time; keep stocks isolated if unwanted

BMTL.name: Breakable Metal

props.tmp: Rust/reactivity countdown. While >1: decrements each frame and has a 1/100 chance per adjacent METL/IRON neighbor to convert it to BMTL, seeding the new BMTL's tmp from itself (clamped to 1 if own tmp<=7, otherwise own tmp minus a random 0-4). While ==1: 1/1000 chance/frame to convert self to BRMT.
props.life: PROP_LIFE_DEC flag is set on this element, but the life field is never read or written anywhere in BMTL.cpp's own code (auto-decrements via the generic engine only).

transitions.when: custom (tmp reaches exactly 1, not a field transition)

reacts.also: self.tmp-- each frame while >1; converted neighbor's tmp is set to 1 (if self.tmp<=7) or self.tmp minus random(0-4) otherwise

behaviour: Spreads a 'rust' chain reaction into adjacent METL/IRON, converting them into BMTL
Rust reactivity (tmp) depletes as it spreads, eventually the chain stalls out
A fully depleted (tmp==1) BMTL particle has a small chance each frame to shatter into BRMT
Breaks under quite mild pressure (>1.0) into a special-transition state (per description: 'can melt and break under pressure')
Conducts electricity and hot-glows; melts to lava at 1273K
builder_notes: GOLD (see GOLD.cpp) can reverse this rust and turn BMTL back into IRON - pair with gold contacts to 'heal' rusted metal
Low pressure tolerance (1.0) makes it fragile in pressurized enclosures compared to plain METL
A single rusted BMTL seed can slowly convert an entire METL/IRON structure it touches

BRCK.name: Brick

props.tmp: When ==1, graphics() renders a blue-shifted fire-glow overlay (FIRE_ADD pixel mode). Nothing in BRCK.cpp itself ever sets tmp to 1 - the trigger for this visual state is not present in this file.

behaviour: No update() function - purely physical, no in-file reactions
Crushes into STNE above 8.8 pressure
Melts to lava at 1223K
Has an unused-in-this-file tmp==1 'glowing overlay' graphics state (source of the trigger is elsewhere)
builder_notes: Structurally weaker under pressure than it looks - 8.8 pressure threshold turns it to loose stone
Good moderate-heat wall material (survives to 1223K)

COAL.name: Coal

props.tmp: Reactivity value, defaults to 50. Forced down to 39 when local pressure>4.3 while tmp>40; otherwise decrements by 1/frame while 0<tmp<40; reaching <=0 converts the particle to BCOL (Broken Coal).

reacts.also: particle becomes FIRE itself

reacts.result: spawns an ember FIRE particle at a random adjacent offset; self.life--
reacts.cond: life<100 (each frame it stays in this 'burning' band)
tmp reaches <=0 (accelerated by local pressure>4.3, which forces tmp to 39 if it was >40)

behaviour: Burns very slowly: spawns ember FIRE particles and depletes its own life while life<100, until life<=0 turns it into FIRE
High local pressure (>4.3) accelerates structural decay (tmp) toward becoming BCOL (Broken Coal)
Has no standard HighTemperature field transition - melting/burning is entirely life/tmp driven in-code
Glows red/orange via graphics() once actual temp exceeds 395.15K (cosmetic only)
builder_notes: A COAL deposit under pressure (>4.3) will break down into BCOL faster than one that just sits idle
Expect ember FIRE particles to appear around burning coal (life<100) - don't assume it's inert while smoldering
No LAVA transition exists for COAL in this file - it only ever ends as FIRE or BCOL

CRMC.name: Ceramic

props.tmp2: Randomized 0-4 at creation; used purely to offset colour brightness in graphics() for visual banding.

transitions.when: custom pressure code (not the LowPressure field, which remains IPL/NT)

AirDrag/AirLoss/Loss are all 0.00 - behaves as a totally airtight, frictionless solid in fluid calculations
Description claims it 'gets stronger under pressure' but no positive-pressure hardening code exists in this file - likely handled by generic Hardness-based engine mechanics elsewhere
Extremely heat-resistant (2887.15K) before special-transitioning
builder_notes: Vacuum/strong-suction environments (pressure below -30) will convert ceramic panels to CLST - check that if a build unexpectedly changes material
No positive-pressure-driven behaviour is coded here despite the description; don't rely on this file for a 'gets stronger' mechanic

DRIC.name: Dry Ice
behaviour: No update() function - purely physical, no coded reactions
Very low default spawn temperature (172.65K) and very low heat conductivity (2)
Sublimates into CO2 gas above 195.65K
Cools ambient air (HotAir = -0.0005*CFDS)
builder_notes: Excellent cold-source/insulated cold pack given its low heat_conduct - slow to warm up
Narrow stable temperature window before subliming to CO2 (only ~23K above its default spawn temp)

GLAS.name: Glass

props.tmp3: Snapshot of local cell pressure*64 from the previous frame; used to compute the frame-to-frame pressure delta that can shatter the glass into BGLA.
props.life: 'Chemical strengthening' level (0 = untreated up to a much higher chemically-strengthened state); raises the shatter-resistance threshold (strength = life/120 + 16, floor 16) and, above ~200, enables the liquid-nitrogen condensation behaviour.

transitions.when: custom pressure-shock code (not the LowPressure/HighPressure fields, which remain IPL/IPH/NT)
transitions.at: |delta(pressure*64) vs previous frame| exceeds strength threshold (16 minimum, higher if chemically strengthened via life)

reacts.also: local cell pressure -= 1.0, self temp += 200K
reacts.cond: life-derived strength>200 (chemically strengthened), own temp<77K, ambient hv<77K, local pressure>5.0

behaviour: Shatters into BGLA when local pressure changes too abruptly frame-to-frame (threshold scales with 'strength'/life)
Chemically-strengthened (high-life) glass below 77K in a >5 pressure, >77K-hv environment condenses liquid nitrogen onto itself (1/100/frame), venting local pressure and warming itself by 200K
Photons and neutrons pass through; hot-glows when heated; melts to lava at 1973K
Sparks are allowed to settle on it (PROP_SPARKSETTLE)
builder_notes: Sudden pressure swings (not just high absolute pressure) are what shatters glass here - pulse-y pressure builds are riskier than steady ones
Raise 'life' (chemical strengthening) to make glass more pressure-shock resistant and unlock the LNTG-condensation trick
The LNTG condensation only triggers in a fairly narrow cryogenic + high-pressure window

GOLD.name: Gold

props.ctype: Set to PT_GOLD when the particle converts to SPRK, so it can revert to GOLD correctly.
props.life: 0 normally; set to 4 when it conducts a spark relayed from a nearby low-life SPRK.

reacts.also: the BMTL's rust tmp is cleared to 0 as it becomes IRON
reacts.cond: axis-aligned neighbor (one of rx/ry is zero) within a random +/-4px sample, checked 8 times per frame
reacts.chance: deterministic per successful sample, up to 8 tries/frame

reacts.also: life set to 4, ctype set to PT_GOLD
reacts.cond: own life==0, SPRK found at one of 4 orthogonal probe points 4px away
a neutron occupies the same cell
reacts.note: Occurs despite GOLD carrying PROP_NEUTPASS (neutrons normally pass through it)

behaviour: Reverses BMTL rust back into IRON on nearby (axis-aligned, up to 4px) rusted metal - matches its 'reverse corrosion of iron' description
Conducts electricity with the same custom long-range (4px orthogonal) spark-relay trick as SLCN
Has a small (1/7 per frame) chance to absorb/destroy a neutron sharing its cell, despite being flagged neutron-passing
Melts to lava at 1337K; subtle per-frame colour speckling in graphics() is purely cosmetic
builder_notes: Use gold contacts near BMTL structures to actively 'heal' rust back into plain IRON over time
Don't assume gold is fully neutron-transparent in practice - it occasionally intercepts one
Effective conduction range extends a few pixels beyond direct adjacency, same caveat as SLCN

GOO.name: Goo

props.life: 0 until triggered by local pressure>1.0, then set to a random value in [300, 379]. While >0, the particle also drifts, adding 0.1x the local air velocity to its own velocity each frame. Reaching 0 kills the particle (PROP_LIFE_KILL_DEC).

behaviour: Sits inert (no drift, no decay) until local pressure exceeds 1.0
Once triggered, gets a 300-379 frame lifespan during which it deforms/drifts along with local air currents
Disappears entirely once its life counter reaches 0 - matches its 'deforms and disappears under pressure' description
Neutrons penetrate it fully (PROP_NEUTPENETRATE)
builder_notes: Not a permanent structural solid under any real pressure - anything above 1.0 pressure starts an irreversible ~300-379 frame countdown to destruction
During its countdown it will physically drift with airflow, so it can migrate out of place before vanishing

HEAC.name: Heat Conductor

transitions.to: NT (no engine transition; comment notes this value is only used by other elements for their own special melting logic)

behaviour: Its own update() bypasses normal diffusion: every frame it samples the 8 points at +/-4px in each 3x3 direction (excluding centre), skipping any point whose line of sight is blocked by a heat-insulating particle
Averages temperature (weighted by heat capacity, via SimulationData::HeatCapacityOf) across itself plus every reachable sampled particle and any photon occupying those cells
Writes that averaged temperature back into itself AND into every contributing sampled cell/photon simultaneously - effectively an instant, line-of-sight-limited heat equalizer over a small radius
Has no type-specific reactions; the equalization applies to any non-insulating particle within range
Cannot melt via ordinary heat conduction (HighTemperatureTransition = NT); its 1887.15K figure exists only for other elements' code to reference
builder_notes: Great for near-instant local heat sinking/spreading, but effective range is capped at 4px per axis and blocked by any heat-insulating material in the line of sight
Since it doesn't transition on its own even past 1887.15K, don't expect it to melt from ambient heat - only other elements referencing HEAC's threshold can cause special effects
Placing insulators between HEAC and a target will silently break the intended heat-sharing path

ICEI.name: Ice

props.ctype: Element ICEI reverts to when it melts (HighTemperature ST-special); defaults to PT_WATR, can be set to PT_FRZW to make the ice continuously self-cool by 1K/frame
props.life: PROP_LIFE_DEC decays each frame; not otherwise read by ICEI's own update()

transitions.to: ST-special: melts into its ctype (default WATR)

reacts.result: neighbor FRZZ becomes ICEI with ctype set to FRZW

behaviour: Static solid (Gravity 0, Advection 0), does not fall or move
Cools surrounding air slightly (negative HotAir)
If ctype=FRZW, self-cools by 1K every frame indefinitely
Crushes into SNOW above 0.8 pressure
Melts back into its stored ctype liquid at 252.05K
builder_notes: Set ctype=FRZW before placing to build a self-refrigerating ice block
Keep pressure below 0.8 or it turns to SNOW
Adjacent SALT/SLTW slowly converts both into SLTW brine over time
Default melt threshold (252.05K) is colder than plain water's 273.15K freezing point

IRON.name: Iron

props.tmp: Not used by IRON itself; after rusting into BMTL, that particle's tmp is set to a random 20-29 rust-shade value
props.life: Rust-immunity counter: while life>0 (decaying via PROP_LIFE_DEC), update() returns immediately and skips all rust checks

behaviour: Static solid, conducts electricity, glows when hot
Melts into LAVA at 1687K
Rusts into BMTL when touching SALT, SLTW, WATR, O2, or LO2

builder_notes: Avoid SALT/SLTW/O2/LO2 contact for corrosion-free iron builds
Plain WATR is nearly safe (~1/1200 chance/frame)
Externally setting life>0 makes an IRON particle temporarily rust-proof

NICE.name: Nitrogen Ice
behaviour: Completely static/passive solid; has no update() function at all, no reactions
Extremely cold default temperature (35K)
Melts directly into LNTG at 63.1K, a very low threshold
Cools surrounding air slightly (negative HotAir)
builder_notes: Even mild ambient heat above 63.1K converts it to LNTG - handle with care
Useful as a pure inert extreme-cold heat sink block

PLNT.name: Plant

props.ctype: Bitfield (see PLNT.h): bit0 = tree-growth-mode flag; bits1-2 phase(2b); bits3-5 direction(3b); bits6-11 colour(6b); bits12-19 growth-life(8b). In ordinary (non-tree) mode, only the colour bits are meaningfully carried between cells.
props.tmp: Ordinary mode: if ==1, this cell is allowed to sprout a VINE onto adjacent WOOD. Tree mode: phase-0 growth program byte (5-bit branch bitmask + 2x2-bit next-phase selectors).
props.tmp2: Ordinary mode: highest temperature (K) recorded above 350K, used only to tint graphics for heat stress. Tree mode: phase-1 growth program byte.
props.tmp3: Tree mode: phase-2 growth program byte. Unused in ordinary mode.
props.tmp4: Tree mode: phase-3 growth program byte. Unused in ordinary mode.
props.life: Ordinary mode: countdown set to rand(60,119) after eating SMKE/CO2 (via PROP_LIFE_DEC); vents O2 to all empty neighbors once it decays to exactly 2, then resets to 0. Tree mode: growth steps remaining before branching/stopping.

reacts.result: neighbor WATR is reborn as a new PLNT particle (same colour, life=0)
neighbor SMKE destroyed; PLNT.life set to rand(60,119)
neighbor CO2 destroyed; PLNT.life set to rand(60,119)
spawns a VINE particle in a nearby empty cell (inherits PLNT's temperature)
reacts.cond: adjacent WOOD, surround_space nonzero, PLNT.tmp==1, random empty offset must be free

behaviour: Ordinary PLNT eats adjacent WATR to clone itself, keeping its colour
Touching LAVA ignites it into FIRE
Absorbing SMKE/CO2 stuns growth for 60-119 frames, then bursts O2 into empty neighbors once when the countdown hits 2 (PLNT.cpp:326-342)
Cells flagged tmp==1 sprout VINE growths onto adjacent WOOD

Tree-growth mode (ctype odd) recursively creates new PLNT cells to build branching trees, finally converting itself into WOOD (thin tip) or GOO+2xWOOD (thick base) once growth life hits 0 or the phase dictates a stop (PLNT.cpp:104-259)
Tree growth only proceeds between 278.15K-343.15K; dies (reverts to ctype=0, loses genome) below 223.15K or above 373.15K; merely pauses (no death) at other out-of-band temperatures (PLNT.cpp:65-79)
A finished tree branch has a 1/10 chance to shoot out a SEED carrying the colour genome (PLNT.cpp:233-249)
Ignites into FIRE at 573K in either mode
builder_notes: Feed with WATR to multiply plant cells across a surface
Keep away from LAVA/open FIRE unless intentional ignition is wanted
For tree builds, seed with ctype odd + genome bits and hold ambient temp 278-343K for continuous growth
SMKE/CO2 exposure only delays a plant cell; it eventually vents O2 rather than dying

PSTS.name: Solid Paste
behaviour: Fully static, passive solid with no update() logic
Solid form of PSTE (paste); reliquefies below 0.5 pressure
No temperature transitions defined (ITL/ITH sentinels = never)

Not directly selectable from the element menu (MenuVisible=0) - only produced by PSTE solidifying

reacts.cond: orthogonal neighbor 4px away carries SPRK with 0<life<4, self not already charged

reacts.result: neighbor shield instantly promoted one tier (SHLD1->2->3->4), life set to 7
neighbor becomes PLUT, emits a PHOT
